articles.title: USDT Buyers Face 22% VAT on Moscow Exchange
articles.text:
USDT buyers face 22% VAT when Moscow Exchange opens crypto trading
Buyers will pay VAT on top of the trade price in December because Russia’s tax code has no explicit exemption for foreign digital instruments.
Buyers of Tether’s USDt (USDT) stablecoin will pay a 22% value-added tax (VAT) on top of the trade price when Moscow Exchange (MOEX) opens crypto trading on Dec. 1, according to the exchange’s clearinghouse.
The National Clearing Centre (NCC) said it would apply VAT to USDT purchases, sales and swaps through Dec. 31. A buyer purchasing 100,000 rubles worth of USDT would pay an additional 22,000 rubles in VAT.
Unlike Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH), which Russia classifies as digital currencies, USDT falls under a separate legal category known as foreign digital instruments. Russia’s tax code excludes sales of digital currencies from VAT, but it provides no explicit exemption for foreign digital instruments, according to the NCC.
The NCC said it had asked Russia’s Federal Tax Service and Finance Ministry for guidance. It said it would update market participants if it received clarification or if lawmakers exempted trades conducted before Jan. 1, 2027.
Bank of Russia rules that took effect Nov. 17 allow non-qualified investors to buy Bitcoin, Ether and USDT through intermediaries, with annual purchases capped at 300,000 rubles (about $3,650) per intermediary.
Related: Sanctions fears loom over Russia’s regulated crypto trading launch

articles.title: Ansem Meme Coin Crashes After $2.57 Million Wallet Drain, Bullpen Confirms Security Breach
articles.text:
In brief
- Crypto influencer Ansem reported that his Solana wallet had been compromised through his account on trading platform Bullpen.
- Blockchain researchers initially questioned his explanation, suggesting the funds had moved between wallets previously associated with him.
- Bullpen confirmed unauthorized transfers affecting early beta users, including Ansem, and took the affected service offline.
Crypto trading platform Bullpen confirmed a security incident on Tuesday after a wallet belonging to popular crypto influencer Ansem dumped millions of dollars worth of meme coins, which led to accusations that the trader had deliberately sold his holdings and blamed hackers.
The incident sent The Black Bull, a Solana meme coin that trades as ANSEM named after the influencer, crashing roughly 60% in less than an hour. An on-chain investigation subsequently identified $2.57 million in funds transferred to a wallet on Arbitrum.
“On November 24, we identified unauthorized transfers involving Bullpen accounts opened during our early beta between April and June 2024,” the company said on X. “Our preliminary count is 18–19 affected accounts, including [Ansem’s].”
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Solana with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
The announcement lends credibility to Ansem's explanation of what happened earlier Tuesday, when blockchain trackers spotted his wallet rapidly liquidating its meme coin holdings.
“Pump wallet is hacked, trying to figure out how, believe its unauthorized access to my bullpen profile somehow which had the sol priv key imported,” Ansem wrote on X.
Bullpen, a crypto trading terminal co-founded by Ansem himself, allows traders to import existing wallets using their private keys. Anyone who obtains that key can effectively take control of the corresponding wallet, signing transactions that the blockchain recognizes as legitimate regardless of who initiated them.
ETH price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
A subsequent investigation by blockchain data provider Bitquery identified moved funds at $2.57 million total, with approximately $2.1 million coming from meme coin sales.
Crypto Twitter wasn't buying it
Ansem's explanation initially met considerable skepticism from crypto traders and blockchain researchers, some of whom pointed to what appeared to be connections between the recipient wallet and the influencer's older addresses.
“Pretty sure Ansem didn’t get hacked lol,” pseudonymous blockchain researcher MLM wrote on X.
“The onchain activity looks nothing like a hack,” he added. “Just an hour before the selling started, a previously inactive wallet I’d labeled as Ansem’s a year ago funded the wallet that later received the sale proceeds.”
A proposed Community Note on Ansem's post went considerably further, accusing the influencer of deliberately liquidating his position and transferring the proceeds to his own wallets. The note even drew a comparison with Haliey Welch, the internet celebrity behind the controversial HAWK meme coin.
The note was still awaiting additional ratings.
Ansem rose to prominence during the 2024 meme coin frenzy thanks in part to his calls on tokens such as Dogwifhat (WIF). Decrypt named him among its rising crypto stars that year, when his following had grown to approximately 600,000 accounts on X.
His namesake token debuted on the Solana meme coin factory Pump.fun in June 2026 after an anonymous developer created the coin and allocated a substantial portion of its supply to the influencer.
There were also reasons to question the accusations against Ansem before Bullpen issued its statement. Bitquery found that an older Solana wallet was emptied around the same time as his main wallet, potentially explaining why an address previously associated with the trader had funded the recipient.
Meanwhile, his Hyperliquid trading account, which held approximately $373,000, remained untouched. Someone with access exclusively to his Solana private keys would not necessarily have access to that account.
Bullpen said the affected accounts represent less than 0.005% of its registered user base. The company has yet to disclose the precise vulnerability, the total losses across affected accounts, or whether it intends to compensate users.
“We’ve taken the affected test service offline,” Bullpen said, adding that it would contact affected users directly and provide updates every three hours throughout the investigation.

articles.title: Swiss Central Bank, UBS and SIX Study Tokenized Settlement
articles.text:
Swiss central bank, UBS and SIX study ledger for tokenized settlement
The study will assess whether a shared ledger can bring central bank money, commercial bank money and securities onto the same platform.
The Swiss National Bank (SNB), UBS, SIX and other financial institutions announced a study Tuesday into whether a shared ledger could settle domestic and cross-border transactions involving tokenized assets.
Other participants include Zürcher Kantonalbank, PostFinance, Banque Cantonale Vaudoise, Basler Kantonalbank, Sygnum Bank and settlement platform Seturion, the central bank said in its announcement.
The proposed Swiss Financial Ledger would bring central bank money, commercial bank money and securities onto one platform. Participants will assess the benefits and risks, compare designs and examine how to govern and operate the ledger. The SNB said the study leaves open whether the ledger will launch or the central bank will issue tokenized money to financial institutions.
The initiative is part of the SNB’s Project Helvetia, which explores how to settle tokenized asset transactions in central bank money.
It also builds on Project Agorá, an initiative of the Bank for International Settlements and the Institute of International Finance, which explores whether tokenization can make wholesale cross-border payments faster, cheaper and safer.
Related: UBS partners with five banks for Swiss franc stablecoin sandbox

articles.title: Europol Traces $28M in Crypto Behind Europe's Illegal Streaming Industry
articles.text:
In brief
- A Europol-coordinated operation traced more than €26 million ($28 million) in crypto transactions linked to illegal IPTV services, with further analysis ongoing.
- Investigators from 11 countries worked with Binance, Coinbase and Chainalysis in Seville, disrupting 57 illegal streaming services and identifying 321 piracy websites.
- Europol said police are increasingly targeting the payments behind piracy services, since taking down a service doesn't necessarily stop the people running it.
Law enforcement agencies from 11 countries have traced more than €26 million ($28 million) in crypto payments linked to illegal TV streaming services, in an operation that brought in crypto exchanges Binance and Coinbase and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, Europol said on Tuesday.
The five-day operation, held at the Spanish National Police headquarters in Seville from November 16 to November 20, 2026, disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services. Investigators also identified 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content, which together receive more than 7.3 million visits a year. Analysis of the crypto transactions is continuing.
Investigators are increasingly targeting the money behind illegal streaming services, not just the services themselves.
Last week, Chainalysis joined Europol, law enforcement from 11 countries, and industry partners including Binance and Coinbase in Seville for a five-day… pic.twitter.com/XqV0Hima26
— Chainalysis (@chainalysis) November 24, 2026
IPTV, or internet protocol television, services sell access to television channels, live sports and films over the internet. Illegal providers charge a few euros a month for unauthorized access to premium content, often taking subscription payments in crypto, according to Europol.
Following the payments
During the operation, investigators traced suspicious transactions across blockchains to find links between illegal services, the crypto wallets receiving payments and the people controlling them.
Europol said the operation reflected a shift in strategy. Rather than focusing only on shutting down streaming services, investigators are increasingly targeting the financial infrastructure behind them, because taking a service offline does not necessarily stop the people running it.
Europol has gone after criminals' crypto in other cases, too. In June 2026, its Operation Endgame froze more than €41 million ($47 million) in crypto linked to infostealer malware, and in March it helped disrupt a proxy network whose payment platform had received more than $5.7 million in crypto.
Around 40 people took part, including 30 law enforcement officers from Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Spain and the U.S.
Europol coordinated the operation through its Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition, a unit supported by the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), which also took part alongside INTERPOL and the Audio-visual Anti-Piracy Alliance (AAPA). The information gathered will feed into national investigations to identify suspects and trace assets.
An estimated 60 million people in Europe use unauthorized IPTV services, costing legitimate providers €4.83 billion ($5.3 billion) a year and governments a further €1.08 billion ($1.2 billion) in lost taxes, according to AAPA figures cited by Europol. Demand appears to be growing: visits to websites offering sign-ups for illegal IPTV services rose 10% in 2023, an EUIPO study found.
Crypto and piracy
Europol ran a similar operation last year. In November 2025, a week-long cyber-patrol in Alicante, Spain, traced about $55 million in crypto linked to piracy services and referred 25 illegal IPTV services to crypto providers for disruption, The Record reported at the time.
Crypto also features in older piracy cases. In Germany, the alleged operator of defunct piracy site Movie2K has been offered a deal to end his money laundering and tax evasion trial if he hands over 40,000 BTC. Prosecutors believe he still holds about 56,000 BTC, bought with proceeds from the site before it shut down in 2013.
The offer came days after German lawmakers approved new powers allowing customs officials to seize crypto and other assets of unclear origin without first opening a criminal case.

articles.title: Sky Community Proposes up to $50M Buybacks to Address stUSDS Liquidity Crisis
articles.text:
Sky lender proposes buyback of up to $50M to fund stUSDS withdrawals
Borrowers would sell SKY to the protocol and use the proceeds to pay down their loans, freeing up funds for depositors in the stUSDS pool.
A lender in Sky Protocol’s stUSDS pool proposed Monday that the project spend $40 million to $50 million of its reserves buying SKY tokens from borrowers to free up funds for depositors who have struggled to withdraw.
Depositors lend USDS, Sky’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, to borrowers who put up staked SKY as collateral. The pool has been at or near full utilization since Nov. 10, leaving depositors reliant on new deposits or loan repayments to withdraw.
The lender, who posts as Conquercube, called for a vote on an over-the-counter buyback. Each sale would use the USDS proceeds to pay down the seller’s loan in the same transaction. Conquercube estimated the buyback could bring utilization down to between 68% and 74%.
Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery found that a wallet linked to Sky co-founder Rune Christensen accounted for 48% of the debt backed by the pool as of Thursday.
Christensen acknowledged Monday that his borrowing contributed to depositors’ difficulty withdrawing. He said he repaid 3 million USDS and still owed about 77 million USDS on loans backed by his staked SKY. To repay the balance, he said he was exploring a direct sale of some of his SKY tokens to institutional investors.
Related: Sky Protocol sees $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals, disputes illicit fund claims

articles.title: Justice Department Moves to Forfeit $1.1B in USDC From North Korea's Binance Hack
articles.text:
In brief
- The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture action for more than $1.1 billion in USDC that it says North Korean hackers stole from Binance and laundered.
- The funds were already under a government-requested restraining order. Circle, which issues USDC, provided "valuable assistance," the department said.
- U.S. authorities say they have helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the October 29 hack, up from $2.7 billion frozen two weeks earlier.
The U.S. Justice Department has moved to permanently take control of more than $1.1 billion in crypto stolen by North Korean hackers in the record $6.4 billion theft from Binance.
The department filed a civil forfeiture claim on Monday for the funds, which are held in USDC, the stablecoin issued by Circle, it said. The assets were already subject to a restraining order the government had requested after the hack, and Circle provided "valuable assistance," the department said.
ETH price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
The filing is part of a wider U.S. effort to help Binance recover the stolen funds. Since the October 29 hack, the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto, according to the department. That is up from the $2.7 billion in frozen assets it reported on November 12, when it said it had court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion.
"Swift coordination between the government and private sector partners helped prevent a substantial portion of those assets from disappearing," Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the department's Criminal Division said in a statement.
Secret Service investigators identified and froze stolen funds "within minutes of the hack," said Todd Bratz, special agent in charge of the agency's Criminal Investigations Division. The Secret Service is investigating the case alongside the FBI and IRS Criminal Investigation.
Laundering continues
The FBI has attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, which the Justice Department describes as members of the North Korean military. North Korea has denied involvement, and Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover customer losses.
Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze funds after the hack. But the hackers have kept moving what they still control. After two weeks of inactivity, wallets tied to the hack began moving Ethereum in mid-November.
At least $247 million has since been funneled through Bitcoin coinjoins, a mixing technique that pools funds to obscure their origin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said on Monday. Elliptic estimates that about $2.85 billion has been frozen and that roughly $2.35 billion remains in addresses tied to the theft.
Binance has also pursued the funds through the courts, winning a $6.5 billion freezing order from Abu Dhabi courts that can be served on wallet holders via the blockchain.

articles.title: Grayscale Calls Bitcoin Oversold at $62K but Warns of AI Risks
articles.text:
Grayscale calls Bitcoin ‘oversold’ at $62K but warns of AI risks
Grayscale said Bitcoin’s bear market was its longest on record at 411 days and counting, though the 56% drop was the smallest percentage decline.
Bitcoin appeared oversold near $62,000 on Monday, while risks tied to artificial intelligence (AI) could dominate its near-term outlook, according to Grayscale Investments.
More than $2 billion flowed out of crypto exchange-traded products worldwide last week, and options traders were paying a premium for protection against further losses, Zach Pandl, Grayscale head of research, said in a Monday blog post.
Bitcoin (BTC) briefly fell below $56,000 on Saturday, its lowest price since September 2024. Pandl said the low put Bitcoin 56% below its October 2025 peak. By his count, the bear market reached 411 days, making it Bitcoin’s longest on record, though the percentage decline was the smallest.
Bitcoin traded at about $60,200, down about 1.7% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko
Pandl said developments in the AI sector could have more influence on crypto prices in the near term than activity on blockchain networks. He pointed to the leadership upheaval at Nvidia and uncertainty over how the US midterm election results could affect data center construction.
“We believe public blockchain fundamentals look solid, and that current valuations offer an attractive entry point for investors with medium- and long-term holding periods,” Pandl said.
Related: Bitcoin dips back under $60K as gold seals worst 60-day loss since 1980s

articles.title: CertiK Trains Interpol Investigators to Trace and Freeze Stolen Crypto
articles.text:
In brief
- CertiK trained law enforcement officers at an INTERPOL cybercrime meeting in Hanoi on tracing stolen crypto across blockchains and getting exchanges to freeze funds.
- Officers followed funds from a real wallet compromise through swaps, bridges and intermediary wallets to three deposit addresses at an exchange.
- CertiK said Web3 security losses reached about $2.6 billion in the first three quarters of 2026, driven by compromised keys, phishing and supply-chain attacks.
Blockchain security firm CertiK trained police investigators from across Asia and the South Pacific in tracing stolen crypto and securing asset freezes at an INTERPOL meeting in Hanoi, the company said.
The 3rd INTERPOL Asia and South Pacific Working Group Meeting on Cybercrime ran from October 27 to October 30, 2026. It was organized by INTERPOL's Cybercrime Directorate and Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security. CertiK said senior law enforcement officials from 20 countries attended, with stablecoin issuer Tether and South Korean exchange Upbit among the other private-sector partners.
Following the money
CertiK's sessions focused on the two stages of recovering stolen crypto: mapping how funds move after a theft, then using that evidence to ask exchanges to freeze them.
Officers worked through a real wallet-compromise case, using open-source block explorers and CertiK's compliance software to follow stolen funds through token swaps, cross-chain bridges and intermediary wallets to three deposit addresses at an exchange. The exercise included spotting address-poisoning decoys, which attackers use to send investigators down false trails.
CertiK's team then explained the process for contacting the exchange, using its law enforcement portal and filing formal requests to freeze the funds.
Other sessions covered how to read wallet activity before and after a suspicious transaction, how smart contract vulnerabilities and audit findings can inform an investigation, and how to tell apart attacks involving compromised signing keys, phishing and social engineering.
"Investigators need both a clear picture of how an attack happened and a practical route to act on the evidence," Esme Pau, CertiK's head of capital markets and policy, said in a statement.
Interpol's crypto crackdown
Fellow security firm Group-IB, which also presented, tweeted that the four-day meeting drew more than 80 participants from over 43 countries and regions. INTERPOL's working group for heads of regional cybercrime units first met in Manila in September 2024.
The training comes as INTERPOL steps up its work on crypto-enabled crime. In July 2026, it said that a 20-year-old Thai suspect's wallet had moved more than $122.5 million in romance-scam proceeds in 10 months, using cross-chain swaps to hide the trail. The case was one of many in Operation First Light, a 97-country sweep that led to 5,811 arrests.
💫 Group-IB participated in the 3rd @INTERPOL_Cyber Asia & South Pacific Cybercrime Working Group Meeting in Hanoi, Vietnam, held from 27–30 October 2026. Led by INTERPOL’s Cybercrime Directorate - Asia & South Pacific Cybercrime Operations Desk and co-hosted by Vietnam’s… pic.twitter.com/tYaKEUnaXL
— Group-IB Global (@GroupIB) November 3, 2026
In October 2026, Operation Serengeti III recovered more than $105 million across 21 African countries and shut two illegal crypto mining centers in Angola. It followed Operation Catalyst, in which INTERPOL and Afripol arrested 83 people in 2025. INTERPOL's member countries also designated scam-compound networks, which channel billions of dollars through crypto, a transnational criminal threat in November 2025.
Tether, which can freeze USDT at flagged addresses, has become a regular partner in such investigations. In April 2026, it froze more than $344 million in USDT across two Tron addresses in coordination with U.S. authorities. Earlier this month, it formed a task force with Tron and Chainalysis to trace illicit USDT on Tron and help police freeze it.
Stablecoins such as USDT remain a concern for investigators. Earlier this month, a UK taskforce convened by think tank RUSI warned that USDT has been linked to Russian-speaking laundering networks, citing a July 2025 HM Treasury report.
$2.6 billion in losses
Pau cited about $2.6 billion in Web3 security losses during the first three quarters of 2026, with compromised keys, targeted phishing and supply-chain attacks among the main causes.
CertiK's H1 2026 report recorded some $1.32 billion lost across 344 incidents, and its security dashboard puts third-quarter losses at $1.28 billion.
That figure predates the largest theft of the year. The FBI has attributed October's $6.4 billion hack of Binance, which took place during the Hanoi meeting, to North Korea's TraderTraitor group. North Korea has denied involvement.

articles.title: South Korea Unveils Draft Bill to Promote Crypto Innovation, User Protection
articles.text:
South Korea proposes bank-led stablecoins, 20% cap on crypto exchange stakes
The draft bill would also reopen domestic initial coin offerings after a ban dating to 2017 and require issuers to disclose risks before soliciting buyers.
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) unveiled a draft bill Tuesday that would initially limit issuance of won-denominated stablecoins to groups majority-owned by banks and generally cap shareholders’ stakes in crypto exchanges at 20%.
Banks would have to own more than half of a stablecoin issuer collectively, though a fintech or technology company could be its largest individual shareholder, the FSC said in its announcement.
Domestic stablecoin issuers would need FSC authorization and at least 5 billion won (about $3.7 million) in equity capital. They would also have to hold reserves covering at least 100% of their outstanding tokens and redeem them at face value without delay.
Exchanges would need dealing, brokerage and custody licenses and would have to meet capital and operating requirements. Shareholders’ stakes would be capped at 20%, or 34% with FSC approval.
The draft also seeks to lift South Korea’s 2017 ban on domestic initial coin offerings.
Regulators previously aimed to produce the bill in 2025, the year President Lee Jae-myung campaigned on introducing a won-denominated stablecoin.
Work stalled over who could issue the tokens. The central bank wanted banks to control issuers, while the FSC favored allowing nonbank companies to issue them as well. The proposed cap on exchange ownership also drew opposition from lawmakers.
Related: South Korea lawmakers mull pushing crypto tax implementation to 2029

articles.title: Morning Minute: Jensen Returns, Markets Soar (Except Crypto)
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors reverse NVDA pump, close lower; BTC at $60.4k
- NVDA board announces Jensen’s return; NVDA jumps 35% (-5% premarket)
- BTC ETFs use brief pump to exit another $570M in outflows
- OKXICE officially launches its tokenized stock trading platform
- Ansem pump wallet seemingly hacked; ANSEM -50%
Jensen Returns, Markets Soar (Except Crypto)
Six days after Nvidia’s board chair told investors “the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” the board voted unanimously to reinstate him as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.
Nvidia shares rose 33% to around $167, adding roughly a trillion dollars of market value in a session. Huang’s personal net worth climbed about $36.6 billion on his 3.5% stake, moving him to 13th on the Forbes global list. Short sellers took roughly $12.2 billion in paper losses, their worst single day since at least 2019, which wiped out the $10.5 billion they had booked the prior week.
The stock market absolutely ripped on the news. The Nasdaq closed up 6.51% at 24,089, its best day since April 2025. The S&P gained 4.7%, the Dow was +3%, and the VIX collapsed 25.8% to 26.62.
Bitcoin went along with the ride—for a few hours. It touched $63,929 intraday, up 5.1%, then spent the afternoon handing it back and finished near $61,000, barely up on the day. The ETFs used the pump to exit more, with BTC ETFs seeing another $570M in outflows on the day.
ETH and other majors also closed red. Alts gave back their gains. And the CMC top 20 index managed just 0.20% gain.
That’s a 19 to 1 ratio between what the Nasdaq captured and what Bitcoin kept, on the same catalyst, on the same day. Pain for the crypto bulls.
What makes it even more painful, is that crypto fell with AI stocks the whole way down, and the standard explanation was that both trade on the same liquidity and the same risk appetite. Monday tested that and the correlation fell through. The AI trade got a catalyst and markets bounced. Crypto didn’t bounce with it.
As for Nvidia’s reversal decision itself, questions remain to say the least. The board says it was satisfied with Huang’s “candor and ability to lead,” and that input from senior U.S. officials left it confident his return “poses no national security risk.” Trump publicly pushed for it and said the board had sought assurance on the espionage allegations. What actually changed between November 17 and November 23 hasn’t been explained. The independent directors’ investigation is still open, and Nvidia is now standing up a board committee for national security and export-control oversight plus recruiting a chief compliance officer.
Perhaps answers will trickle out over time. The AI trade may not need them anyway. And crypto, well, it's in its own world right now, waiting for its own catalysts (likely quantum-related). But it’s very unclear that catalyst is coming in 2026, and it’s becoming clear that many are not interested in waiting for the answers…
🌎 Macro, Crypto and Markets
- Crypto majors are red and reversing the NVDA pump gains; BTC -1.6% at $60.4k; ETH -1% at $1,700; SOL -3% at $70.7 HYPE -2% at $62.5; ZEC -7% at $735
- ATOM (+8%), VET (+3%), Stable (+2%) and Morpho (+3%) led top alt movers

articles.title: Bitcoin Dipped on Huang’s Nvidia Exit but Jumped 5% on His Return
articles.text:
Bitcoin dipped on Huang’s Nvidia exit but jumped 5% on his return
Bitcoin rose about 5% on Jensen Huang’s return, more than the 3.5% it lost on news of his exit, but remained 19.2% below its pre-resignation price.
Bitcoin fell 3.5% the day Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO and jumped about 5% on news of his return Monday before giving back the gain by the US stock market close. CoinMarketCap
Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $59,740 at 10:38 am UTC Tuesday, according to CoinMarketCap, still 19.2% below its Nov. 11 close of $73,928, the day before Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation.
Meanwhile, Nvidia (NVDA) shares rose over 31% on Monday to close at $165, according to Yahoo Finance. Earlier on Monday, the company’s board announced reinstating Huang as president and CEO of Nvidia.
Australian trading firm Neo-X described Bitcoin’s jump on the Huang news as the kind of move where “venue depth thins and a single-venue price runs ahead of the market.” Its trading desk pointed to withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin funds as one reason the gain faded, saying “Monday’s rally did nothing to reverse that flow.”
On Oct. 29, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, of passing information to Beijing. The Financial Times later reported that US officials believed she and Jensen Huang were romantically involved. China denied the spying allegation.
On Nov. 11, the Times reported a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice president who reported directly to Huang. The board accepted his resignation that day.

articles.title: GTA 6 PC Ports ‘Nuked’ Just Days Before Devs Expected It to Be Playable
articles.text:
In brief
- The Leonida GitHub project and the GTA6Modding Discord, two of the most serious efforts to port GTA 6 to PC, have shut down.
- The takedowns came a day after Cyberleek released the leaked Xbox build's executable, which devs thought made a playable PC port just days away.
- Other servers in the AI-powered porting scene have locked down, and some members have moved to more private platforms.
Several major projects attempting to port Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC have been "nuked," according to community insiders. It comes as developers thought a playable port was just days away, after notorious Rockstar hacker Cyberleek released the game's files.
Both the Leonida GitHub page and the GTA6Modding Discord server—two of the most serious attempts at porting the latest Grand Theft Auto title to PC—have been removed. Other servers also involved in the AI-powered porting scene, such as the Chasm Server, have also locked down.
"Leonida and GTA6Modding have both been nuked," Freakman, a Chasm Server mod, wrote on Discord. "We have no affiliation with Cyberleek," they added. "Multiple servers have been struck, we're staying low for tonight."
Cyberleek released an Xbox build of GTA 6 on November 19, the day the game launched on consoles. However, they held back the main executable needed to run it and promised they'd release it if the CYBERLEEK meme coin hit a $15 million market cap.
Porting projects had been preparing for that file, expecting it'd be the key to making the port playable. The scene leans heavily on AI coding tools to speed up the reverse engineering needed to get console games running on PC, with developers describing themselves as "vibe coders."
The meme coin missed its $15 million target, but Cyberleek released the executable on Monday anyway. The next day, several GTA 6 porting projects were shut down.
"They're taking out servers left and right that are mentioning the leak," Chasm community member Weedgoose told Decrypt. "Some servers take the hit while others are going dark and are waiting for the flames to extinguish."
Which movie will be the highest-grossing movie of 2026?
Some of the impacted community members have moved to alternative messaging platforms that are more private than Discord, Weedgoose said.
It appears the Leonida GitHub was removed by its creator, an apparent high school student, as it shows a 404 error page rather than a DMCA takedown page. That said, there's no way of knowing if the creator received a cease and desist (or similar correspondence) that led to this decision.
Chasm mod Freakman did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment regarding why the server has gone dark.
Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, has been going after the leaks for months. In August, it filed subpoenas asking Discord and Microsoft, which owns GitHub, to hand over data that could help identify Cyberleek.
Rockstar has yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6 yet. GamesBeat reported in October that one could arrive in Q1 of 2027—and the prospect of an unofficial port releasing in advance of that would likely dent sales.
Rockstar did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.

articles.title: Bitcoin Gives Back Gains as Long-Term Holders Exit With 33% Losses
articles.text:
Bitcoin dips back under $60K as gold seals worst 60-day loss since 1980s
Bitcoin continued to threaten the loss of $60,000 support as gold attempted to bounce from a 60-day losing streak during which it fell nearly 25%.
Bitcoin (BTC) dipped below $60,000 on Tuesday after rallying Monday on news that Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.
Key points:
- Bitcoin fell nearly 8% from its intraday high of $64,505 as 24-hour crypto liquidations hit $827 million.
- Gold fell 24.6% over the 60 days to Nov. 23, marking its sharpest 60-day decline in 44 years.
- Analysis warned that long-term Bitcoin holders selling at a loss could limit future rebounds.
BTC price fails to hold $64,500 rebound
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD falling to $59,380 on Bitstamp, down nearly 8% from its intraday high.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
News of Huang’s return sparked a rally in crypto and stocks at Monday’s Wall Street open, with Nvidia shares rising as much as 35%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed 6.5% higher at 24,089.
On Tuesday, the stock rally spread to Asia, where enthusiasm over the improving prospects of the AI trade spread to Asia, where South Korea’s Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) gained 6.3% after posting its lowest close in 11 months.
KOSPI daily chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The Kobeissi Letter forecast a “bumpy road” for the sector.
“Over the coming days, there will likely be a ton of political headlines in what has become one of the most pivotal CEO controversies of all time. And, the broader AI trade is still experiencing growing pains as it undergoes a healthy technical correction,” it wrote on X.
“However, we continue to believe that what has materialized over the last few weeks is a mere correction, not the beginning of a prolonged bear market.”
Relief was visible beyond stocks as gold gained as much as 1.6% on Monday, after posting its lowest daily close since September 2025.
XAU/USD one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Gold fell 24.6% in the 60 days to Monday, its steepest 60-day decline since 1982, according to analyst Lukas Kuemmerle. Gold remained 35% below its January all-time high of $5,602 per ounce.
“What we see is a domino effect. A liquidity event that started in AI stocks is pulling cash out of every market, so commodities fall across the board, no matter what their fundamentals say,” he wrote on Monday.
XAU/USD sell-off comparison. Source: Lukas Kuemmerle/Substack
Long-term Bitcoin holders sell at a loss
Bitcoin, meanwhile, failed to hold its own rebound. Crypto liquidated $348 million in long positions and $478 million in short positions over the 24 hours to 8am UTC as markets gyrated, according to CoinGlass.
Related: BTC price gains 12% from $55K: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Crypto liquidations vs. BTC/USD chart (screenshot). Source: CoinGlass
A contributing analyst at onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant warned that long-term Bitcoin holders selling at a loss could limit future rebounds.
As Bitcoin climbed to $64,500, long-term holders — entities holding a given unit of BTC for at least 155 days — took an average loss of 33%. The cohort’s Spent Output Profit Ratio (SOPR) hit 0.67 after dropping to 0.64 on Friday, its second-lowest reading of 2026.
“Capitulation from long-term holders has historically appeared near local bottoms, but it is a process rather than a single print,” the analyst wrote.
Bitcoin LTH-SOPR chart. Source: CryptoQuant
Cointelegraph previously reported newer Bitcoin investors accoutned for the largest share of realized losses earier in November.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post Record $4.71B in November Outflows So Far
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs keep bleeding as BlackRock’s IBIT shares gain nearly 5%
BlackRock’s IBIT shares gained 4.85% on Monday despite continued Bitcoin ETF withdrawals that pushed November’s net outflows to $4.71 billion.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) extended their outflow streak to five consecutive trading days amid a rebound in shares of the largest Bitcoin fund, BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).
The funds recorded $569.7 million in net outflows on Monday, bringing November’s total so far to $4.71 billion, according to SoSoValue data. The withdrawals have surpassed June’s record of $4.51 billion, putting the funds on track for their worst month since launching in January 2024.
IBIT shares gained 4.85% on Monday to close at $34.62 before slipping 1.3% in overnight trading, Yahoo Finance data showed. Meanwhile, Bitcoin (BTC) fell 1.8% over 24 hours to around $60,450, erasing Monday’s rally following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded $2.37 billion in net outflows over the past five trading sessions, led by IBIT’s $1.95 billion in withdrawals. The BlackRock fund broke its daily outflow record twice last week.
Bitwise’s Camran Khosravi attributed IBIT’s record outflows to a broader retreat from risk assets amid tech and artificial intelligence sector concerns and hawkish Federal Reserve signals.
“The largest funds naturally see the largest flows in both directions, and even record daily outflows are small relative to their total assets,” Khosravi told Cointelegraph.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs held $73.6 billion in combined net assets as of Monday, with IBIT holding $45.64 billion, according to WalletPilot data.
Related: Institutions pile back into US Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 after selling streak

articles.title: $14.7B in ‘Lost’ Bitcoin Has Moved Since 2018: Report
articles.text:
In brief
- Of 92,076 Bitcoin wallets that a developer listed as dormant in 2018, 9,990 have since moved some 245,000 BTC, worth just over $14.7 billion.
- The findings come as a New York lawsuit seeks to have 39,069 dormant Bitcoin addresses, including wallets linked to Satoshi Nakamoto, declared abandoned property.
- Some wallets named in the suit have since moved funds, and one pseudonymous holder has filed to dismiss the case, claiming to still control a named wallet.
Bitcoin that hasn't been moved in years is sometimes considered "lost" by industry onlookers, and one lawsuit is arguing that they've been "abandoned." But since 2018, roughly 10,000 supposedly lost Bitcoin wallets have sprung back to life.
Pseudonymous developer Quickben22 built a list in 2018 of 92,076 Bitcoin wallets that hadn't moved funds in more than six years, assuming the owners had lost their keys. Eight years later, the developer revisited the list to discover that 9,990 of those wallets have since moved a total of approximately 245,000 BTC, or just over $14.7 billion at Bitcoin's current price.
"Dormant is not the same as lost," Quickben22 told Decrypt. "I expected nearly all of the 92,076 addresses to still be silent after 8 years. About 89% are, but 9,990 have moved, and 14+ year old addresses are still waking up."
That distinction matters, as the findings come as a New York lawsuit brought by a pseudonymous plaintiff known as 'Noah Doe' tries to claim 39,069 dormant Bitcoin addresses as abandoned property, including wallets linked to Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto.
The plaintiffs argue the coins are "abandoned" under New York's lost property law. They say they found the wallets, reported them to the NYPD, and sent the owners notice by attaching on-chain messages to tiny Bitcoin transactions.
"It's like writing down the addresses of every locked house on a street, telling the police, and claiming whatever is inside because nobody answered the door," Quickben22 said.
Some wallets linked to the suit have since woken up, with several moving funds earlier this year—including one first funded in 2013 that shifted 411.45 BTC in October, then worth $33.4 million. One pseudonymous holder has also filed a motion to dismiss the case, claiming to still control a named wallet.
Quickben22's list was originally built for an app called Bitcoin Key Hunter, which guesses private keys at random and checks them against the dormant addresses in the hope of landing on one.
"It's like playing the lottery, but with much, much smaller odds," he said, before breaking down the math: roughly 1 in 10^43 across the whole list. "Those are about the odds of winning five Powerballs in a row," he added.
Quickben22 did not respond to Decrypt's query on whether he has successfully guessed the keys to any of the listed wallets.
BTC price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
It is impossible to know who exactly moved the funds from the supposedly lost wallets—it might not even be the original owner. An original owner tidying up old funds looks the same on-chain as someone who found a seed phrase in a drawer, or a hacker who got hold of a key that was never theirs.
"The blockchain shows that someone could sign, but not who," Quickben22 wrote.
Hunting lost Bitcoin
Even when a wallet really is lost, the owner doesn't always let go.
Welshman James Howells has spent more than a decade trying to recover a hard drive holding around 8,000 BTC, which his then-girlfriend accidentally threw out during an office clear-out in 2013. He traced it to a landfill in Newport, Wales, and spent years seeking permission to dig it up, until a judge dismissed his case on environmental grounds. Howells called the ruling a "stitch-up."
Last year, he offered the local council £2.5 million to buy the landfill outright, Decrypt reported. The council didn't respond. He has since given up the search and is instead launching Ceiniog, a Bitcoin layer-2 network with a token he says is backed by the buried coins he can't access.
“MY view is this: As long as YOU (or anyone else in the world) can view the balance [and can] verify for yourself that it still contains 8,000 Bitcoin, then [the] Ceiniog coin is fully backed with its value,” he told Decrypt last year. “If those coins ever moved, Ceiniog instantly loses its backing and value. I am guaranteeing that those coins will never move—because the private key is on a [hard drive] in a landfill.”
Howells' 8,000 BTC haven't moved since 2013. On paper, they look exactly like the coins on Quickben22's list, and the kind the Noah Doe lawsuit wants declared abandoned.

articles.title: Trump Says He 'Made the Deal' to Reinstate Jensen Huang, Sparking Bipartisan Backlash
articles.text:
In brief
- President Trump said he "convinced" Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang, telling CNBC the administration assured directors that Huang posed no national security threat.
- Republicans including Sen. Tom Cotton and Sen. John Cornyn joined Democrats in questioning the decision, and Sen. Elizabeth Warren demanded to know who gave the board "input."
- Trump's own Nvidia stake may have gained up to $15 million on Monday's rally, according to an analysis of his disclosures by the Financial Times.
U.S. President Donald Trump has taken credit for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, drawing criticism from lawmakers in both parties who say the administration has yet to explain what assurances it gave the company's board.
"I convinced them," Trump told CNBC in a phone interview on Monday, shortly after Nvidia reinstated Huang as president and CEO. "I made the deal."
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Trump said the board had asked for assurances that Huang was not a national security threat, and that the administration provided them based on "everything we know." He said a government investigation had found that Huang himself was exonerated. Asked whether last week's stock losses had shaped his view, Trump said "probably so."
The board's decision was sealed by a personal promise from Trump on Sunday, CNBC reported, citing three people familiar with its thinking. Senior administration officials had contacted directors overnight on Friday, and Huang then joined meetings with the board over the weekend, the outlet said. The board's statement cited input from "senior levels of the United States government" without naming anyone.
Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Saturday that Huang was not the target or subject of any Justice Department investigation, and that there was no evidence he had broken laws, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials.
During a marathon board session on Sunday, Huang disclosed additional affairs beyond the two that had been widely reported, but was contrite, the newspaper said, citing people familiar with the discussion.
Trump told The New York Times that he had consulted Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton before recommending Huang's return. "I had to go to them before I recommended this," he said. A day earlier, Clayton had said that the U.S. investigation into Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, was ongoing.
The reversal came six days after board chair Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to bring Huang back. Trump later posted an AI-generated image on Truth Social showing Huang holding a red bra aloft in his raised fist, in a pose modeled on the photo of Trump after the 2024 assassination attempt on his life.
Backlash from both parties
Huang's reinstatement drew the ire of lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.
"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement. She called on the administration to explain what input was given, and by which officials.
Republicans also pushed back. Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR), chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, tweeted that the controversy over Nvidia and Megaspeed was "not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back," and pledged to pass chip export-control bills including his Chip Security Act.
I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access. The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back.…
— Tom Cotton (@SenTomCotton) November 23, 2026
"No national security risk? Based on what?" Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) tweeted, quoting the board's statement. Sen. John Curtis (R-UT) asked who in government had weighed in and what they told the board, noting that it had ruled out Huang's return only a week earlier. "I'd like to know what changed," he wrote.
Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) tweeted that Huang's behavior "does not support reinstatement," adding that Nvidia still had to answer for national security concerns and "unaccounted-for chips."
Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), who is expected to become House Speaker in January, called the board's decision "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible" in a statement. He promised an investigation into Nvidia and into what he called "corrupt abuse of power" by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his department.
Trump's Nvidia stake
Trump's own Nvidia holdings may have gained as much as $15 million in value on Monday, according to the Financial Times, which calculated that he could have held up to 370,000 shares as of September 30, based on his latest ethics disclosure. At the low end of the disclosure's ranges, he would have held about 32,000 shares and gained $1.3 million. The White House did not respond to the newspaper's request for comment.
Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) tweeted that the president was "selling out our national security to keep the stock market high," calling for an investigation into stock trades made before the announcement.
Nvidia shares closed up 31.5% at $165.05 on Monday, adding about $950 billion to its market value, before slipping 5% to $156.82 in premarket trading on Tuesday, according to Yahoo! Finance.
Huang is due to sit for a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 1, and to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3. On Monday, the Commerce Department also added Megaspeed to its Entity List trade blacklist.

articles.title: Why 42 Macro Is Waiting to Buy the Bitcoin Dip
articles.text:
Why 42 Macro says it’s waiting to buy the Bitcoin dip
The independent macro research company warns the Bitcoin sell-off may not have yet run its course.
Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, says his firm has trimmed its Bitcoin exposure and is waiting for signs that the sell-off has run its course before it considers buying again.
“We’ve already de-risked out of Bitcoin,” Dale said in an interview with Cointelegraph last week. “Our stress levels are low. We’re just waiting to buy.”
Dale’s comments came just days before Bitcoin fell to a two-year low around $55,100 on Saturday, raising questions about whether Bitcoin has finally found its bottom this cycle.
However, Dale warned that persistently high inflation could prompt further Fed tightening that could drain the liquidity that supports Bitcoin. The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to increase rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting on Dec. 9.
“Bitcoin doesn’t generate earnings. Bitcoin needs liquidity to go up,” he said.
Bitcoin was trading at around $64,000 at the time of the interview. Dale said it could fall another 30% to 40% if the S&P 500’s decline from its Oct. 6 peak reaches 20% by Christmas, which would put it at around $38,400. The S&P500 is currently down 7.4% from that peak.
Related: Bitcoin rebounds 17% from $55K lows as Nvidia rally sparks $500M crypto liquidations
Asked when 42 Macro may consider buying Bitcoin again, Dale said the firm will be looking at its own market signals.
“And once we pivot to a risk on market regime, once Bitcoin, the bottoming process concludes and our signals go from bearish right now to neutral or maybe even back to bullish. That’s when you want to buy.”
42 Macro sees a Fed pivot lifting Bitcoin in 2027
Despite near-term caution, Dale expects the conditions to become more favorable for Bitcoin around the middle of 2027, when easing inflation could give the Fed room to shift away from tighter monetary policy.
“So we think 2027 will be a phenomenal year for stocks, gold, Bitcoin,” he said.
Dale said the Fed may need to see second-quarter inflation data before changing course, putting the potential shift in late June or in the first half of the third quarter.
