articles.title: Rời xa những khuôn mẫu quen thuộc: Người trẻ đang định nghĩa lại sự "đủ"?
articles.text:
Những năm gần đây, khái niệm về một cuộc sống viên mãn của giới trẻ đang có nhiều thay đổi. Thay vì bó buộc bản thân trong những cột mốc vật chất cố định, nhiều người chọn cách tận hưởng từng khoảnh khắc và tìm kiếm niềm vui từ những trải nghiệm tinh thần đa dạng.
Trong nhịp sống hiện đại, người trẻ có nhiều cơ hội tiếp cận với những phong cách sống và hình thức giải trí khác nhau. Một kỹ năng, khoá học, chuyến du lịch, một buổi hòa nhạc hay đơn giản là khoảng thời gian thư giãn bên bạn bè đều có thể trở thành niềm vui đáng giá. Vì vậy, thành công không nhất thiết phải gắn với những cột mốc lớn lao mà nằm ở cách sống và sở thích của riêng mình. Với mỗi người, sự đủ đầy có thể mang một ý nghĩa riêng và đôi khi chính những điều bất ngờ nhỏ bé lại tạo nên gia vị thú vị cho cuộc sống thường nhật.
Với một sinh viên mới tốt nghiệp, sự hài lòng có thể đơn giản là tìm được công việc yêu thích và từng bước khẳng định bản thân. Với người mới đi làm, đó có thể là được trải nghiệm nhiều hơn, khám phá những vùng đất mới hay theo đuổi một sở thích đã ấp ủ từ lâu. Trong khi đó, với người đã có cuộc sống ổn định, sự đủ đầy đôi khi lại nằm ở những khoảnh khắc bình dị bên gia đình và những người thân yêu.
Những hoàn cảnh và góc nhìn khác nhau tạo nên những hình dung đa dạng về sự đủ đầy. Dù chỉ mang tính minh họa, những ví dụ này cho thấy giá trị của cuộc sống không chỉ nằm ở một khuôn mẫu cố định, mà ở cảm xúc tích cực mà mỗi người tìm thấy trong từng trải nghiệm thường ngày. Vì thế, "bao nhiêu là đủ?" không có một đáp án chung cho tất cả. Điều đáng quan tâm hơn là cách mỗi người đón nhận những niềm vui bất ngờ và biến chúng thành khoảnh khắc thư giãn đáng nhớ.
Một góc nhìn thú vị về quan niệm này có thể được tìm thấy qua sự quan tâm của người chơi đối với các giải thưởng Jackpot của hai sản phẩm xổ số tự chọn Mega 6/45 và Power 6/55. Trong đó, Mega 6/45 có giá trị Jackpot khởi điểm từ 12 tỷ đồng; Power 6/55 có Jackpot 1 khởi điểm từ 30 tỷ đồng và Jackpot 2 khởi điểm từ 3 tỷ đồng. Những mức giải thưởng khác nhau mang đến nhiều sự quan tâm và hình dung riêng của người chơi về niềm vui nếu may mắn trúng thưởng. Tuy nhiên, mỗi người có một cảm nhận khác nhau về giá trị của giải thưởng, cũng như những mong muốn riêng trong cuộc sống.
Power 6/55 và Mega 6/45 là hai sản phẩm xổ số tự chọn có giá trị Jackpot cao nhất của Vietlott.
Là sinh viên mới tốt nghiệp đại học, chị Thùy Linh (Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh) cho biết thỉnh thoảng chị ghé điểm bán Vietlott gần nhà để mua vài tờ xổ số tự chọn Power 6/55. Theo chị, sức hút của sản phẩm không chỉ đến từ giá trị giải thưởng mà còn nằm ở sự hồi hộp khi theo dõi kết quả quay số và chờ đợi vận may.
"Mình thấy Power 6/55 khá thú vị vì giải thưởng có nhiều mức khác nhau. Thỉnh thoảng rảnh rỗi mình ghé mua vài tờ, chủ yếu là để trải nghiệm cảm giác chờ kết quả. Nếu có cơ hội may mắn trúng thưởng, 3 tỷ là vừa đủ để khởi nghiệp một quán trà sữa nhỏ, vừa là thoả đam mê lại vừa có thêm một thu nhập ngoài công việc văn phòng", chị Linh chia sẻ.
Nếu chị Linh yêu thích cảm giác hồi hộp khi chờ đợi kết quả, thì với chị Thu Quỳnh, một chủ doanh nghiệp nhỏ, việc mua xổ số tự chọn lại là một hoạt động giải trí mà hai vợ chồng thỉnh thoảng cùng trải nghiệm. Chị cho biết gia đình thường lựa chọn Mega 6/45 và cũng có những hình dung riêng về niềm vui nếu một ngày may mắn nhận được giải thưởng Jackpot.
"Hai vợ chồng mình thỉnh thoảng cùng mua Mega 6/45 vì thấy sản phẩm có cách chơi khá đơn giản. Mỗi lần mua, cả hai cũng hay đùa với nhau về việc nếu may mắn trúng thưởng thì sẽ làm gì, mua xe hay sửa lại nhà cho bố mẹ trước. Với mình, điều vui nhất đôi khi chỉ là có thêm một chủ đề để hai vợ chồng cùng trò chuyện và chờ đợi kết quả", chị Thu Quỳnh chia sẻ.
Hai câu chuyện với những góc nhìn khác nhau cho thấy mỗi người có một cách cảm nhận riêng khi tham gia xổ số tự chọn. Với người này, đó là sự tò mò và hồi hộp khi chờ kết quả; với người khác, đó là một trải nghiệm giải trí có thể chia sẻ cùng người thân. Những cảm xúc ấy cũng phần nào phản ánh cách mỗi người tìm kiếm niềm vui trong cuộc sống thường ngày.
Giá trị Jackpot của xổ số tự chọn Power 6/55 và Mega 6/45 luôn hấp dẫn người chơi xổ số.
Với xổ số tự chọn Mega 6/45 và Power 6/55, các giải thưởng Jackpot là một trong những yếu tố tạo nên sự quan tâm của người chơi. Tuy nhiên, mỗi người vẫn có những kỳ vọng và cảm nhận riêng khi tham gia. Cũng như quan niệm về thành công trước tuổi 30, sự đủ đầy không nhất thiết phải gắn với một con số hay một khuôn mẫu cố định. Vậy với bạn, điều gì mới thực sự tạo nên một cuộc sống đáng mong đợi?
Để biết thêm các thông tin khác về xổ số tự chọn Power 6/55 và Mega 6/45, người chơi có thể theo dõi trên trang web chính thức của Vietlott: https://vietlott.vn/
Người chơi cũng có thể tìm hiểu thông tin về kênh phân phối xổ số qua điện thoại của Vietlott (ứng dụng hỗ trợ Vietlott SMS) tại đây: https://info.vietlott-sms.vn/.

articles.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
articles.text:
The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it’s investigating a “cybersecurity incident.” The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it’s looking into an “incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” It hasn’t offered any information about the full scope or source of the breach, but FinCEN has taken some systems offline as a precaution.
US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.
The news comes hours after The New York Times reported that the Central Intelligence Agency and Office of the Director of National Security discovered a breach of an open source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information. The Department of Defense, whose National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency was also reportedly impacted by the breach, declined to comment. The CIA and ODNI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s unclear if the FinCEN breach is related. Americans have been on high alert about security incidents after a series of seemingly unrelated outages earlier this month.
Americans have been on high alert about security incidents
FinCEN’s role is to protect the financial system from illegal activity, including by combatting money laundering and terrorism financing. The bureau maintains financial transaction data and distributes it for law enforcement purposes. FinCEN also houses reports of suspicious activity that financial institutions file as part of the Bank Secrecy Act.
FinCEN says in its alert that banks can still file reports about suspicious activity online, but some services may not be immediately available. Filers that need to expedite their reports in the meantime can still call the Financial Institutions Hotline, which it says was not impacted by the disruption.
Update, November 24th: Added response from Department of Defense.

articles.title: 5 different types of gadgets and accessories you'll want in your car
articles.text:
5 different types of gadgets and accessories you'll want in your car
Stay safe, charged up and organized.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
There are few things more annoying when driving than when you can't find something that you're looking for, whether that's your phone, sunglasses or those mints you sorely need. The good news is that most of these annoyances are easy to fix and don't require spending an absolute fortune.
Car gadgets and accessories have become practical ways to make your daily commute better and overall calmer. You can't influence traffic, but you can make life inside your car more convenient. Some will improve safety by letting you keep your eyes on the road, while others will provide comfort, protection against the elements or simply keep your car from turning into an expensive junk drawer.
We'll take a look at a few categories of car gadgets and accessories that address common issues drivers have, including phone mounts and dashboard organizers, dash cams and blind spot mirrors, power solutions, climate and visibility enhancements, as well as organization and storage tools.
Phone mounts and chargers
You get in your car, throw your phone somewhere in the center console or on the passenger seat, and the first serious stop of the day will send it flying. Then you find yourself trying to fish it off the floor while driving — and that's seriously dangerous. Since so much of modern driving involves your smartphone, whether we're talking about navigation, calls or music, where the phone sits matters. Therefore, a phone mount that keeps your device in a stable and visible spot will cut down on how often you glance down or fumble to grab it.
There are multiple types of phone mounts you can get. Some clip onto the air vent, others use suction mounts attached to your dash or windshield, while others take over an unused cup holder as a base. If your phone comes with wireless charging and MagSafe or a compatible case, magnetic phone mounts with wireless charging are also an option.
Whether it's because your own phone is constantly running out of power or your kids are burning through their tablets' batteries, wired in-car charging solutions are always good to have on hand too. These days, you can grab chargers that plug into your car's 12-volt cigarette lighter sockets and accommodate multiple cables. If your car already has USB ports, you could also get some longer cables that reach the backseat or shorter ones that you can use for your own phone up front. Charging devices in the car, by the way, has negligible effects on fuel economy.
Try to get braided cables since those don't tangle as easily and are generally more durable. You might also want to look into a multi-tip charging cable so you can power up multiple devices, like older iPhones with Lightning ports or ancient tablets with micro-USB ports.
Comfort and organization
There are more things you can get to keep your dashboard organized. No one likes the sun beaming straight into their eyeballs, so sunglass mounts are a must. Many cars come with a dedicated cubby for glasses, but you can always buy clips that let you hang your shades from your sun visors. Some come with little magnets, and they're easy to operate with a single hand, while others are literal pouches. You could also grab little trays specifically made for your car's dashboard where you can put things like parking passes. Given their location, however, it's best to be careful about what you put in there because anything metallic, like coins or keys, could turn into dangerous projectiles in the event of an accident.
Other useful in-car storage solutions are car seat gap fillers that go between your seat and the console so nothing slips through that space. You can also install a little trash can that hangs off your console, or that slips into a free cup holder so you have a place for all your food wrappers.
In the trunk, cargo nets and trunk organizers keep groceries, tools or sports equipment from tipping every time you turn a corner. Aside from making it so you don't jump every time you hear a bump in the trunk, you're also going to have an easier time with groceries if you don't have to hunt for every potato that's rolled out of the bag. Back seat organizers hang over the back of your front seats, offering pockets for snacks, toys and tablets for the kids, while hooks that go under the headrest make it possible to hang your bag or backpack.
Surveillance and visibility
These days, you absolutely need a dash cam that records continuous footage of the road. With how crazy traffic can be, having proof that an incident isn't your fault is always a good idea. The most affordable and basic options offer front-only recording, but if you want to pay a bit more for more coverage, you can grab a front-and-rear setup that adds a second camera pointing out of the rear window. There are also systems that point a camera at passengers too. Keep in mind that rules around dash cam placement and recording can vary by state, so it's worth confirming what's allowed where you live and drive before installing one.
Another inexpensive purchase you can make to improve your safety on the road, especially if you drive an older model car that doesn't come with blind spot monitoring, is a set of blind spot mirrors. These small, convex mirrors can cost as little as $10, glue to your side mirrors in about a minute, and widen your field of view, making lane changes safer and easier.
In case of emergency
You also want to ensure you have an emergency kit that includes a seatbelt cutter and window breaker (these are often integrated into a single, two-in-one tool) within reach when you're driving, for scenarios in which you need to escape the car at all costs. You should also have a reflective warning triangle and high-visibility vest somewhere in your car, alongside a first aid kit, fire extinguisher, and an LED flashlight.
Jumper cables should always be stored in your trunk, or you can even get a battery-powered jump starter so you don't need to wait around for another car to help you out. Before buying anything, you have to ensure that the jump starter is rated for your car's engine size and electrical system. You might also want to look for some extra features, as some double as flashlights and USB power banks.
You'll also want to get a portable air compressor so you can handle common roadside headaches like a slow tire leak or a tire that's simply underinflated. These run off either your car's 12-volt outlet or an internal battery, and some models can even automatically shut off once whatever it's inflating hits a preset PSI.
Entertainment and comfort
If your car already has an infotainment touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, great, but if you have an older model car, you can actually add aftermarket CarPlay and Android Auto screens. You plop one on your dashboard, hook it up to some power, connect it to your car's audio system, connect your phone, and use it to view your navigation app, stream music, and so on like you would in a much newer vehicle. Some even feature a built-in dashcam on the back. For the rear passengers, you can add phone and tablet holders to the backs of your front seats, which usually mount to the headrest posts and grab the gadgets in a clamp.
Cabin air quality is another area that's easy to overlook. Car air purifiers are a bit bigger than a coffee mug, feature HEPA filters and some even let you put in fragrances as an added benefit. Your life behind the wheel will also be a lot more comfortable if you cover your windshield with a sun shade whenever you leave your car parked outside during the summer.

articles.title: Threads comes to iPad and takes a page from X's playbook with cashtags
articles.text:
It may have taken 15 years for Instagram to launch on the iPad, but Instagram’s other app, Threads, has taken a slightly faster path to the Apple tablet. In an overnight update, the company rolled out a big-screen version of the X competitor. It’s also added another new feature, borrowed from X: the stock-tracking feature known as cashtags.
While the iPad version of the app works well in portrait orientation, some users are disappointed to find that the landscape layout doesn’t work as they’d expect. Instead of offering a multi-column interface as on Threads’ web app, the iPad app focuses on the user’s main feed in a single-column layout. There are also options to swipe right and left from the main screen to access the search screen and the feeds menu, respectively.
The iPad app isn’t the company’s only update in the latest release. According to a post from Threads engineer Guy Dickinson, Threads will now support cashtags — a feature popularized by Twitter years ago for tracking live stock information. These specialized tags start with the dollar sign (“$”) followed by a ticker symbol. When you click on a cashtag, you can follow the discussions around the stock.
In addition, Threads is adding live stock quotes, charts, and other context at the top of each cashtag’s page. As you search for a particular cashtag, the autocomplete search results will display the stock’s current price and the percentage it’s up or down. Dickinson says the feature will currently support NYSE and Nasdaq stocks, ETFs, and crypto. Cashtags will be supported on the web, iOS, and Android. However, they’re just now rolling out, so you may not immediately see them.
The update points to Threads’ broader ambition to compete with X, not only as a destination for discussions about various topics, but also as a place where people can track real-time news and information. Cashtags in particular could attract traders and investors to Threads who typically rely on X.
Despite facing stiff competition from X, Meta announced earlier this year that Threads topped 500 million monthly users, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg says the company believes the app is on track to reach a billion users over time.

articles.title: Anthropic lets MCP servers ship skills and run background jobs in Claude
articles.text:
Anthropic has opened Skills over MCP in public beta, letting apps that connect to Claude ship playbooks alongside their tools. Tasks, for long background jobs, and Elicitation, which pauses for user input, are now generally available, with File Uploads coming soon.
Apps that plug into Claude through MCP can now also tell it how to use them, Anthropic said on Tuesday. The feature, Skills over MCP, is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code.
MCP is the open standard Anthropic launched two years ago to link AI agents to outside apps and data. Servers built on it already list the tools Claude can use. With skills, they can also ship step-by-step guides and best practices, which Claude loads only when needed.
Shopify uses skills to help Claude design and update online stores, and HubSpot to onboard customers. Skills update with the server, so users have nothing extra to install. More apps are opening up, too: Canva opened its MCP server to all developers on Tuesday.
The beta is on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans. Team admins can switch it on, and Enterprise support is coming soon.
Two other features are now generally available. Tasks lets a server run long jobs in the background while Claude keeps working, which ZoomInfo uses for deeper research. Elicitation lets a server pause and ask the user for input.
GitHub, for example, makes users type a repository’s name before an agent deletes it. Supabase confirms costs before creating a paid project. A fourth feature, File Uploads, will soon let Claude send PDFs, spreadsheets and images to servers.
The features are part of MCP, so servers that support them also work in other compatible apps. Anthropic says MCP now sees over 700M SDK downloads a month. In August, OpenAI and four rivals agreed on a standard for packaging skills and MCP servers.
Skills carry risks, too. That same month, researchers found malicious agent skills that stole passwords and keys after about 1.7 million installs.

articles.title: The reasons why you should never ignore your car's software updates
articles.text:
The reasons why you should never ignore your car's software updates
Hitting "remind me later" every time that pop-up appears may be keeping your car less secure.
Your car isn't just metal and moving parts anymore. Modern cars are more like "smartphones on wheels," with dozens of electronic control units running everything from the infotainment screen to the engine and the driver-assistance systems. All of that runs on software, and software has bugs. On a phone, a bug means an app crashes. On the road, it can mean a backup camera that won't turn on when you shift into reverse, or even a car that brakes when it shouldn't. That's why you should probably stop pressing "Remind me later" every time your car asks to be updated.
A software update is a new version of the code that runs on your car's computers, and it can change a lot more than the look of the touchscreen. Updates might clear up glitches, false warnings, and trouble connecting to your phone. They may patch security holes that could let someone attack a connected car. They can adjust things like engine or battery management, and they can sometimes add features. Some even change how the car drives. After Consumer Reports found braking problems with the original Tesla Model 3 in 2018, for example, Tesla sent out an update that shortened its braking distances.
Sometimes called over-the-air or "OTA" updates, revised software is also how many recalls get fixed now. When a safety defect is in the software, the automaker still has to issue a recall, but the repair can arrive as an update instead of a trip to the dealer. Ford, GM, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and others have done this. Tesla's recall of more than 2 million cars over Autopilot safety controls was fixed that way, with a free update sent wirelessly to owners.
Why skipping updates is a bad idea
Skipping an update means you keep the bugs it was meant to fix, and if it carries a recall fix, that fix never gets installed. Experts say the risks that come with not updating are more significant than the potential issues that come with updating. And that putting updates off can mean missing features and more trips to the dealer, which could ultimately make the car less safe.
Security patches work the same way, and they're often invisible to owners, which makes them easy to ignore. Car hacking has happened before. In 2015, hackers remotely took control of Chrysler vehicles and shut them down, and Chrysler had to recall 1.4 million cars, with the patch delivered on a USB stick. Tesla fixed a separate, similar Model S hack by sending an update to every owner over the air.
Your warranty can be at stake too. GM's 2025 and 2026 warranty booklets require owners to install over-the-air updates within 45 days of availability, and say damage that results from not installing them isn't covered. Tesla and Lucid have similar exclusions. Policies differ by brand (Nissan's 2025 booklet goes the other way and says owners don't pay for parts damaged by an update Nissan delivers), so it's worth checking your own.
How to check for updates and install without drama
Many updates arrive over the air, through the car's built-in cellular connection or a password-protected Wi-Fi network, and they usually show up as a prompt on the infotainment screen. If you've been tapping "later," look for an update option in the car's settings menu. Some automakers require a telematics subscription for over-the-air access, so owners without one, such as some Hyundai and Kia drivers, may need to visit a dealer, sometimes for a fee. Older cars without wireless connectivity can still be updated at a dealership, where a technician may reprogram a control module with diagnostic equipment.
Read the release notes before you start the update. Vague wording like "general improvements" is common, so call the manufacturer if you want details. Install when you won't need the car, with nobody inside and a strong signal or Wi-Fi. Some updates take just a few minutes while others can take up to 90, and many lock the car so you can't drive it. Electric cars may need a charged battery, and some gas cars have to stay running. If an update stalls, moving the car to get a better signal can help, and the dealer is the fallback.

articles.title: Bền bỉ giữ nghề nước mắm, nữ chủ hợp tác xã đạt doanh thu 15 tỷ đồng/năm
articles.text:
Theo cha học nghề từ năm lớp 7, khởi nghiệp với vài chục chum nước mắm
Ở tuổi 54, bà Đặng Thị Luận, trú tại phường Hải Ninh (trước đây thuộc thị xã Kỳ Anh, Hà Tĩnh), thường xuyên có mặt tại khu sản xuất để kiểm tra từng mẻ nước mắm.
Cơ duyên với nghề làm nước mắm của bà Luận bắt đầu từ khi còn học phổ thông. Cha bà là ông Đặng Văn Bứu, từng làm kỹ thuật viên tại Trạm nước mắm Kỳ Ninh. Từ năm học lớp 7, bà đã theo cha đến nơi làm việc vào những ngày nghỉ, quan sát cách chọn cá, pha muối và ủ chượp.
Những kiến thức được truyền dạy khi ấy trở thành nền tảng để bà gắn bó với nghề suốt nhiều thập kỷ.
Năm 1993, sau khi lập gia đình, bà Luận bắt đầu làm nghề thu mua hải sản. Công việc giúp bà tiếp xúc thường xuyên với nguồn nguyên liệu, đồng thời tích lũy thêm kinh nghiệm về chế biến thủy sản.
Đến năm 1996, bà bắt đầu sản xuất nước mắm trên phần đất của gia đình ở vùng biển Kỳ Ninh, với khoảng 30-50 chum sành. Không có nhiều vốn, cũng chưa có hệ thống phân phối, bà chủ yếu làm theo phương pháp được cha truyền dạy rồi tự mang sản phẩm đến bán tại các chợ trong vùng. Khách hàng ban đầu phần lớn là người dân địa phương, sản lượng còn nhỏ và thu nhập chưa ổn định.
Để duy trì khách hàng, bà Luận thường xuyên lắng nghe nhận xét về hương vị sản phẩm, từ đó điều chỉnh cách lựa chọn nguyên liệu và quá trình chế biến. Tuy nhiên, đặc thù của nghề làm nước mắm khiến việc mở rộng sản xuất không thể diễn ra nhanh chóng.
Theo bà Luận, muốn có nước mắm ngon, trước hết phải chọn được cá tươi, phối muối đúng tỷ lệ và quan trọng nhất là không được nóng vội.
Cá sau khi trộn muối phải được đưa vào chum sành, ủ ít nhất 15 tháng. Một số mẻ cần gần hai năm mới đạt yêu cầu. Điều đó đồng nghĩa vốn đầu tư nguyên liệu bị đọng trong thời gian dài, trong khi chi phí sản xuất và sinh hoạt vẫn phải duy trì.
Với số vốn ít ỏi, bà Luận chọn cách tích lũy đến đâu đầu tư thêm chum đến đó. Khi khu đất gia đình không còn đủ diện tích, bà làm đơn xin chính quyền thuê thêm mặt bằng để mở rộng nơi sản xuất.
Đến những năm 2000, hoạt động kinh doanh dần đi vào ổn định. Mỗi năm, cơ sở sản xuất khoảng 200-300 chum nước mắm. Thị trường tiêu thụ được mở rộng, nguồn thu tốt hơn giúp bà có điều kiện tái đầu tư nguyên liệu, thiết bị và tăng quy mô.
Biến cố thị trường và bước chuyển trong sản xuất
Năm 2016, bà Luận cùng 7 thành viên thành lập Hợp tác xã Thu mua và Chế biến thủy hải sản Chiến Thắng. Mục tiêu là tổ chức thu mua hải sản trực tiếp từ ngư dân, chủ động nguồn nguyên liệu và phát triển hoạt động chế biến.
Tuy nhiên, cũng trong năm này, sự cố môi trường biển miền Trung xảy ra, khiến hoạt động khai thác, tiêu thụ thủy sản và sản xuất các mặt hàng chế biến tại Hà Tĩnh chịu ảnh hưởng nghiêm trọng.
Theo bà Luận, thời điểm đó, nước mắm sản xuất ra rất khó tiêu thụ do tâm lý e ngại của người mua. Trong khi đó, nguyên liệu đã thu mua vẫn phải đưa vào sản xuất, hàng tồn kho ngày càng lớn. Nhiều lô sản phẩm phải tiêu hủy, vốn liếng tích góp qua nhiều năm bị ảnh hưởng nặng nề. Tổng thiệt hại lên đến hàng tỷ đồng.
Để duy trì hoạt động, bà sử dụng một phần khoản tiền bồi thường được nhận, đồng thời vay thêm ngân hàng để bổ sung nguồn vốn. Sau thời gian xoay xở, từ năm 2018, hợp tác xã từng bước khôi phục sản xuất, tìm kiếm lại khách hàng và điều chỉnh phương thức chế biến.
Một trong những thay đổi đáng chú ý là tập trung vào dòng nước mắm cá cơm thay vì sản xuất từ nhiều loại cá như trước. Hợp tác xã cũng chủ động tìm hiểu kỹ thuật mới, đầu tư máy móc nhằm giảm sức lao động, tiết kiệm chi phí nhưng vẫn giữ phương pháp ủ chượp truyền thống.
Nguồn cá cơm được thu mua từ ngư dân địa phương. Sau khi lựa chọn, cá được phối trộn với muối theo tỷ lệ phổ biến một phần muối cho 5-6 phần cá rồi đưa vào chum sành hoặc bể để ủ trong thời gian dài.
Bà Luận thường chọn các tháng 2, 3 và 4 để bắt đầu muối cá cơm. Đây là thời điểm nguồn nguyên liệu dồi dào, thời tiết có nắng, thuận lợi cho việc phơi và ủ chượp.
Với dòng nước mắm đặc biệt có độ đạm 34, thời gian hoàn thiện có thể kéo dài hơn hai năm. Để kiểm soát chất lượng, mỗi chum đều được ghi rõ ngày sản xuất và số tàu đánh bắt, qua đó theo dõi nguồn gốc nguyên liệu.
Năm 2022, hợp tác xã đầu tư hơn một tỷ đồng xây dựng cơ sở sản xuất mới trên diện tích một ha tại thôn Tam Hải 2. Bên cạnh hệ thống chum sành truyền thống, đơn vị đưa vào sử dụng các bể nước mắm ứng dụng năng lượng mặt trời, góp phần giảm công lao động và chi phí.
Nỗ lực mở rộng thị trường cũng bắt đầu mang lại kết quả. Năm 2023, khoảng 50.000 lít nước mắm của hợp tác xã được xuất khẩu sang Nga và Angola. Đến cuối năm 2025, đơn vị tiếp tục đầu tư hàng tỷ đồng cho dây chuyền chiết rót nhằm nâng năng suất, đồng thời bảo đảm chất lượng đồng đều giữa các sản phẩm đóng chai.
Theo bảng xếp hạng Top 17 sản phẩm nước mắm được đánh giá cao trên thế giới do TasteAtlas cập nhật ngày 18/11, nước mắm Luận Nghiệp đứng thứ 15, đạt 4,7/5 điểm. "Tôi chưa bao giờ nghĩ sản phẩm có thể đi xa đến vậy", bà Luận nói.
Hiện nước mắm Luận Nghiệp có giá bán từ 45.000 đến 200.000 đồng/chai, tùy dung tích. Việc kinh doanh không còn phụ thuộc hoàn toàn vào các chợ truyền thống như những ngày đầu.
Con trai bà đảm nhận quảng bá sản phẩm trên mạng xã hội và các sàn thương mại điện tử, mở rộng khả năng tiếp cận khách hàng ngoài địa phương.
Theo bà Luận, nhiều người sau khi sử dụng đã trở thành khách hàng thường xuyên, đặt mua qua xe khách hoặc dịch vụ bưu điện. Có người gọi điện chia sẻ đã quen với hương vị nước mắm Luận Nghiệp nên khó chuyển sang sản phẩm khác.
Tháng 4/2026, nước mắm Luận Nghiệp được công nhận đạt OCOP 5 sao cấp quốc gia. Hiện HTX có hơn 3.000 chum sành và khoảng 100 bể ủ nước mắm. Sản lượng nước mắm đạt khoảng 400.000-500.000 lít mỗi năm. Doanh thu của hợp tác xã đạt khoảng 15 tỷ đồng/năm.
Ngoài nước mắm, HTX còn sản xuất ruốc mặn, sứa muối, cá mờm rim lạc và thu mua thủy sản của ngư dân địa phương. Cơ sở tạo việc làm cho khoảng 30 lao động, trong đó 9-10 người làm việc thường xuyên, với mức lương 7-10 triệu đồng/người/tháng.
Trao đổi với PV VietNamNet, đại diện UBND phường Hải Ninh cho biết, cơ sở sản xuất nước mắm của bà Đặng Thị Luận là một trong những cơ sở làm nước mắm gia truyền có quy mô lớn trên địa bàn. Hoạt động sản xuất, kinh doanh của cơ sở góp phần tiêu thụ hải sản cho ngư dân và tạo sinh kế cho người dân ven biển.

articles.title: Electric truck startup Harbinger gets financing boost from Palmer Luckey's bank
articles.text:
Harbinger has tapped Palmer Luckey’s Erebor Bank as a new source of capital as the electric truck startup looks to diversify how it funds its growth and an expanding portfolio of products spanning autonomous vehicles, energy storage, and defense.
Los Angeles-based Harbinger said Tuesday it secured more than $100 million in financing, including a convertible note from Pinegrove Venture Partners and senior debt from Erebor Bank, which launched in February 2026 and recently surpassed $1 billion in loans, according to the Financial Times.
The new financing comes less than three weeks after Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D funding round co-led by Tiger Global, Capricorn’s Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. FedEx, which ordered 2,000 trucks from Harbinger, also participated.
Harbinger co-founder and chief executive John Harris explained in a statement that building an industrial technology company at scale requires a “different financing approach,” adding that the capital needed to ramp up production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn’t have to come entirely from equity. Harris noted that major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations.
Erebor is now Harbinger’s primary banking partner. In a statement, Luckey said traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and creating U.S. jobs.
“Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology,” he said.

articles.title: You can now DM Meta’s Muse on Instagram to turn saves into plans
articles.text:
Meta has added its Muse AI agent to Instagram direct messages, inviting users to send it a DM to turn saved posts into plans, such as a trip. Muse already worked in its own app, in WhatsApp and on Instagram profiles, and Meta says it does not read private messages unless users allow it, though Reuters reported staff found it reading encrypted chats.
Meta’s Muse AI agent can now be messaged in Instagram DMs, where it can turn posts users have saved into plans. Meta announced the change through Muse’s own Instagram account on Tuesday, using a long-planned trip as the example.
Muse launched in the US in September as an agent that books, buys and negotiates for users. It works in its own app and in WhatsApp, and later that month users could add it to their Instagram profiles.
The DM option puts Muse where the saved posts already sit. Meta has not said which countries get it. Beyond the US, Muse is live in Canada and has launched in Australia, and it reached the UK this week.
Messaging Muse does not give it access to private chats. Meta’s privacy page says Muse does not read private messages unless users allow it through a connector.
Yet Reuters reported last week that Meta staff found Muse reading encrypted messages. Meta called those isolated incidents.
Users can also make Muse ask before it sends messages or buys anything. In September, though, a YouTuber said Muse shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before asking him. Meta said it was looking into it.

articles.title: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
articles.text:
The US Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated.
Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
What material is the Army planning to detonate?
There are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. The US started using lead azide as a primary explosive almost a century ago before “moving away” from it about 15 years ago because of how difficult the material is to store and transport, Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), said in a Tuesday press briefing. At that point, the US transferred its remaining stockpile of lead azide to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Lead azide will explode at 350 degrees Celsius (662F). But it is also sensitive to flame, friction, or sudden shock, including fluctuations in temperature.
Some of the material on site in Iowa is more than 60 years old. The material can crystallize as it degrades over time, becoming unstable enough to explode even at ambient temperatures. The Army noted some deterioration of the material in 2009 — but not any “dangerous crystallization” at the time, according to Cekada.
“It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”
The chemical was stored in liquid form, embedded in sawdust and burlap bags inside the drums. Water and ethanol were also added to the containers to keep the lead azide from freezing in the winter. But during a March inspection, Cekada said ATF noticed “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels.” That made the material too unstable for them to open the barrels to add more water and ethanol, Cekada said. Removing a lid might cause the barrels to detonate.
Why is the Army detonating it now?
Officials have been trying to figure out what to do with the crystallized lead azide since that alarming March inspection. The Army initially hired a contractor to safely dissolve the chemicals but canceled the contract earlier this year, according to reporting by The New York Times. Using a chemical neutralization agent “proved to be an unsafe method,” Army Col. Aaron Teller, commander of the 71st Explosive Ordinance Disposal Group, said at the Tuesday briefing, because crystallization on the outside of the barrels made it too risky to open the lids.
“Everyone that we’ve spoken to through their experience has determined that this is the only safe path forward,“ Cekada said at the briefing. If they leave the chemicals as is, he said, they’re still at risk of exploding. “It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”
What are the risks?
Compared to an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion, a controlled detonation is supposed to limit the amount of lead dust unleashed on surrounding communities and the environment. Still, the dust plume could reach as far as 100 miles away from the site. The Army has released maps showing where lead dust is expected to travel based on its modeling.
The last time the Army disposed of lead azide this way at a comparable scale was in 1977, according to Teller. At the time, they detonated 7,000 pounds of the material in Colorado in open air “with zero mitigation.” Even then, 75 percent of the lead particulate stayed on site, Teller said at the briefing. The Army now believes it can “significantly reduce” the spread of that last 25 percent of lead using walls made up of four 16,000-gallon water tanks to capture lead particulate and hopefully prevent it from escaping into the atmosphere.
The 80-year-old earth-covered magazines holding the lead azide are cracked and deteriorating, Teller noted, and they are likely to break open after the detonation. To prepare, they’ve covered it with tarp and a special containment screen for lead. They also plan to flood it with 2 feet of foam to capture particulate pollution. Adam Telle, Acting Secretary of the Army, also said the Army has set out “state of the art gel blocks in huge quantities all around to ensure that we absorb as much of this blast as we possibly can.”
There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead
Last week, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club sought a court order to stop the explosion from taking place, pending an Environmental and Health Impact Statement and an investigation into alternatives to detonating the material. President Donald Trump chimed in on social media, calling for a pause until a federal appeals court gave the Army the green light after previously granting a temporary stay. The court on Monday denied the emergency motion to stop the explosion, clearing the way for the Army to move forward.
What precautions can people nearby take?
The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (Iowa HHS) recommends that anyone in potentially affected areas stay indoors and keep windows shut for 24 to 48 hours after the detonation. Iowa HHS also suggests switching off HVAC systems that might bring outdoor air inside or set them to modes that recirculate air, and using an air purifier with a HEPA filter.
FEMA is helping relocate Middletown residents and others within a voluntary 5-mile evacuation zone. People who are pregnant, children, and individuals with chronic diseases should evacuate the affected areas, Sean Kaufman, principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response at the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, said at the briefing. “Outside of that area, if you’re close to that proximity and you’re uncomfortable, I think you need to do what you need to do to take care of your family,” Kaufman said.
There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead, a neurotoxin that poses health risks when inhaled or ingested. Kids are at increased risk because their brains are still developing and are also more likely to touch contaminated surfaces and then stick their fingers in their mouths. But most adverse health effects — which can include fatigue and gastrointestinal upset alongside impacts on brain development — are connected to chronic lead exposure rather than as a result of a one-off event.
“It is likely this exposure will not result in any observable acute clinical signs,” Will Sander, associate professor of preventive medicine and public health at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, says in an email to The Verge. “Overall, the risk is minimal, and there should be no long-term concerns.”
What happens after the explosion?
“The Army has done this before a long time ago and took lead measurements afterward that were low but hazardous (in my opinion),” Chris Kohler, an adjunct instructor at Indiana University who is an expert on hazardous waste, environmental remediation, and chemical hygiene, says in an email to The Verge. “The detonation will spread lead in the atmosphere. Not a desirable outcome.” Kohler and other experts say it’ll be important to continue monitoring the explosion site and surrounding areas to see if there needs to be any more remediation.

articles.title: Giá vàng SJC đắt hơn thế giới 22 triệu đồng, chênh giá mua bán kỷ lục: Rước rủi ro
articles.text:
Giá vàng hồi phục, khoảng cách trong nước - thế giới lên 22 triệu đồng
Trong phiên giao dịch sáng 23/11 tại thị trường châu Á, giá vàng giao ngay có thời điểm tăng gần 100 USD/ounce, tương đương khoảng 2,7%, sau khi mất 230 USD/ounce trong tuần trước. Đà hồi phục tiếp tục diễn ra khi lực cầu bắt đáy xuất hiện quanh vùng 3.500 USD/ounce.
Tuy nhiên, giá vàng trong nước tăng chậm hơn đáng kể so với thế giới. Vàng miếng SJC được các doanh nghiệp điều chỉnh tăng khoảng 1,5 triệu đồng/lượng, lên 130 triệu đồng/lượng chiều mua vào và 135 triệu đồng/lượng chiều bán ra.
Đáng chú ý, khoảng cách giữa giá mua vào và bán ra đã bị kéo giãn mạnh. Chênh lệch giữa giá mua vào và bán ra tại nhiều doanh nghiệp đã được nới lên khoảng 5 triệu đồng/lượng đối với vàng miếng SJC. Với vàng nhẫn, khoảng cách này cũng ở mức cao, dao động tùy thương hiệu và có nơi lên tới 6 triệu đồng/lượng.
Đây là mức chênh lệch rất lớn, khiến người mua vàng phải đối mặt với nguy cơ thua lỗ ngay khi vừa giao dịch. Chẳng hạn, nếu mua vàng SJC ở mức 135 triệu đồng/lượng, người mua sẽ lập tức chịu khoản chênh lệch 5 triệu đồng so với giá doanh nghiệp sẵn sàng mua lại, chưa kể khả năng giá vàng tiếp tục giảm.
Đến 15h20 ngày 23/11, giá vàng giao ngay chỉ còn tăng khoảng 70 USD/ounce, tương đương 2%, lên 3.612 USD/ounce, quy đổi khoảng 112,5 triệu đồng/lượng. Như vậy, giá vàng miếng SJC bán ra cao hơn thế giới khoảng 22,5 triệu đồng/lượng.
Khoảng cách này đã tăng mạnh so với mức chênh khoảng 10 triệu đồng/lượng cách đây vài tháng, cho thấy rủi ro không chỉ đến từ biến động giá vàng quốc tế mà còn từ mức định giá cao của thị trường trong nước.
Thông thường, khi giá vàng thế giới biến động mạnh, doanh nghiệp kinh doanh vàng có xu hướng nới rộng chênh lệch mua - bán để phòng ngừa rủi ro. Tuy nhiên, động thái này cũng phản ánh sự thận trọng của các đơn vị kinh doanh trước triển vọng giá vàng chưa thực sự ổn định.
Với người mua ở thời điểm hiện tại, có ba rủi ro đáng chú ý: giá vàng trong nước cao hơn thế giới 21-23 triệu đồng/lượng; chênh lệch mua - bán lên tới 5-6 triệu đồng/lượng; và giá vàng quốc tế vẫn đối mặt với nhiều yếu tố bất lợi.
Xu hướng hồi phục thận trọng
Đợt hồi phục của vàng ngày 23/11 chưa đủ để khẳng định thị trường đã hình thành đáy. Sau khi giảm khoảng 9% trong tuần trước, mức giảm mạnh nhất trong 8 tháng, kim loại quý đang chịu tác động đan xen từ chính sách tiền tệ Mỹ, biến động chứng khoán và nhu cầu trú ẩn.
Áp lực lớn nhất hiện nay đến từ Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed). Đồng USD đang ở vùng cao nhất kể từ đầu tháng 4/2025, trong khi lợi suất trái phiếu chính phủ Mỹ duy trì ở mức cao. Kỳ vọng Fed tăng lãi suất thêm 0,25 điểm phần trăm trong cuộc họp ngày 8-9/12 đang tạo sức ép đáng kể lên vàng, tài sản không mang lại lợi suất.
Nếu Fed tiếp tục phát tín hiệu thắt chặt tiền tệ, đồng USD và lợi suất trái phiếu có thể tăng thêm, khiến vàng trở nên kém hấp dẫn. Một số chuyên gia cảnh báo, nếu lạm phát Mỹ tiếp tục dai dẳng, kỳ vọng thắt chặt chính sách tiền tệ có thể kéo dài sang năm 2027.
Marc Chandler, Giám đốc điều hành Bannockburn Global Forex, cảnh báo vàng đang tiến sát mục tiêu giảm 3.500 USD/ounce. Nếu xuyên thủng vùng này, giá có thể lùi tiếp về 3.430-3.450 USD/ounce.
Một yếu tố khác là nguy cơ điều chỉnh sâu trên thị trường chứng khoán Mỹ, đặc biệt ở nhóm cổ phiếu công nghệ và AI. Trong phiên 20/11, chỉ số Nasdaq Composite giảm 5,28%. Cổ phiếu Nvidia mất khoảng 14%, còn AMD giảm hơn 13%.
Khi thị trường chứng khoán bán tháo, nhà đầu tư có thể phải thanh lý cả vàng để bù đắp thua lỗ, đáp ứng yêu cầu ký quỹ hoặc thu hồi tiền mặt. Điều này lý giải vì sao bất ổn tài chính không phải lúc nào cũng khiến vàng tăng giá ngay lập tức.
Tuy nhiên, triển vọng dài hạn của kim loại quý vẫn có những điểm tựa. Nợ công Mỹ ngày càng lớn, nguy cơ mất cân đối tài khóa và những bất ổn địa chính trị, đặc biệt là căng thẳng Mỹ - Iran, có thể tiếp tục thúc đẩy nhu cầu đa dạng hóa tài sản và tìm kiếm nơi trú ẩn.
Bên cạnh đó, nếu làn sóng bán tháo chứng khoán khiến lợi suất trái phiếu giảm, vàng có thể được hưởng lợi. Nhu cầu mua vàng của các quỹ đầu tư và ngân hàng trung ương cũng là những yếu tố cần theo dõi trong trung và dài hạn.
Về kỹ thuật, vùng 3.500-3.558 USD/ounce được một số nhà phân tích theo dõi như khu vực hỗ trợ gần. Ở chiều ngược lại, vùng 3.800-3.900 USD/ounce có thể là khu vực kháng cự nếu giá tiếp tục hồi phục. Việc giá vẫn nằm dưới những đường trung bình này cho thấy xu hướng giảm trung hạn chưa bị phá vỡ.
Nhìn chung, vàng có thể tiếp tục hồi phục trong ngắn hạn nhờ lực cầu bắt đáy và nhu cầu trú ẩn, nhưng chưa có đủ cơ sở để khẳng định một chu kỳ tăng mới đã bắt đầu. Đặc biệt, với mức chênh lệch trong nước - thế giới hơn 22 triệu đồng/lượng và khoảng cách mua - bán lên tới 5-6 triệu đồng, người mua vàng trong nước đang phải chấp nhận mức rủi ro cao hơn đáng kể so với thị trường quốc tế.

articles.title: Uber and Lucid start testing fully driverless rides for their robotaxis in San Francisco
articles.text:
Uber and Lucid start testing fully driverless rides for their robotaxis in San Francisco
The companies are planning to launch their robotaxi service to the public in Q1 2027.
The Lucid-manufactured robotaxis Uber revealed at CES earlier this year are almost ready to give rides to the public. Uber, Lucid and Nuro, the company that developed the autonomous driving system powering their vehicle, have announced that they've started full driverless testing on the public roads of San Francisco Bay Area. They'll soon also give their employees rides on the autonomous vehicles, as well, ahead of their planned public launch in the first quarter of 2027.
While the companies presented the vehicle, a modified Lucid Gravity, at CES earlier this year, they announced the global robotaxi program way back in July 2025. In fact, they've been testing with a driver behind the wheel since December last year. They're now moving to the next phase after securing a California DMV Driverless Testing Permit in May, which gives them the permission to test on public roads in the state without a driver behind the wheel.
Their program's Lucid Gravity vehicles are equipped with high-res cameras, LIDAR sensors and radars, and they're powered by the Nuro Driver end-to-end autonomous driving system. Initially, the tests will be conducted on the roads of Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale, before expanding to more Bay Area cities next year. Lucid said its fleet of robotaxis already consists of 100 vehicles, but it's unclear if they'll all be part of the test's initial rollout.
The companies are planning to launch their robotaxi service in the Bay Area in the first quarter of 2027, with passengers being able to summon the autonomous rides through the Uber aoo. Uber has committed to purchasing 35,000 Lucid-Nuro robotaxis and intends to expand their availability around the world. The ride-hailing company will be designing the vehicle's in-cabin experience and will provide support and rider controls for them when it adds them to its network.

articles.title: Google will make AI agents use new gateways to reach Gmail and Drive
articles.text:
Google has made its Workspace MCP servers and CLI generally available and says AI agents must use them instead of existing REST APIs from February 1, 2027. Every call is checked against company policies, sensitive actions need user confirmation, and a new addendum bars AI tools from training on Workspace data.
Google will require AI agents to reach Gmail, Drive and other Workspace apps through new, dedicated gateways, it said on Tuesday. Regular apps can keep using Workspace’s existing APIs, but agents must switch by February 1, 2027.
The gateways are Workspace MCP servers, which use a common standard for linking AI tools to apps, and a command-line tool. Both are now generally available. Google put an early CLI version on GitHub in March.
Google says its APIs were built for apps that work at human speed, where a valid login meant the user wanted the action. Agents act on their own at machine speed. So every request now gets checked against company permissions and data-loss rules.
Agents can draft emails and summarise documents on their own. But they need a person’s sign-off before sending email, changing Drive sharing or making bulk edits.
Each agent also needs its own sign-in ID with tight limits and usage quotas. Google already gives its Gemini coworker agents their own accounts. It will begin billing for that usage on April 1, 2027.
A new AI Tools Addendum adds rules on data. AI tools cannot use Workspace data to train models or build rival services, and cannot scrape it. They must also delete it when a user disconnects.
Google also tells developers to screen for prompt injection, hidden commands in emails or files that can hijack AI agents. Some controls are still to come, including letting users see and revoke agents’ access themselves.
Other firms are drawing lines too. In October, Charles Schwab said it blocks outside agents from moving client money.

articles.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
articles.text:
Instagram users can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the company announced on Tuesday. The social media network says users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs.
The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content.
Users can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.
Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app.
Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore.
Meta also announced that users can now do more with the posts and reels they’ve bookmarked on Instagram. For example, they can ask Muse to organize their saved content into custom folders, known as Collections. They could also ask Muse to turn a recipe video into a grocery list, turn the travel content from their favorite travel creators into an itinerary for an upcoming trip, or have Muse send them outfit ideas based on fashion reels they’ve collected.
Starting Tuesday, when users save a post on Instagram, they will see a prompt for Muse to organize it for them. This feature is launching in the U.S. and Canada.
Meta says that users remain in control of their Muse experience on Instagram. Nothing is shared, published, or sent without their approval, and they can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions at any time.

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
articles.text:
A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.
The Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.
In total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, violating US sanctions, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The company was acquitted of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Huawei’s sentencing is set for September 14th, 2027, where it may face “financial penalties including criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution,” according to the DOJ.
“For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception,” Tysen A. Duva, the assistant attorney general of the DOJ’s criminal division, says in a statement. “Huawei’s crimes threatened the U.S. financial system, took advantage of American companies that compete honestly in the global telecommunications market, and undermined our national security.”
In a statement to NBC News, a Huawei spokesperson said the charges are “without legal or factual merit” and that it plans to appeal the decision. Huawei didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.
Update, November 24th: Added information from the DOJ.

articles.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
articles.text:
Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.
Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.
Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services, said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.
Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, said on X.
The company said that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.
“It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried,” the company said in a post.
Meanwhile, music labels are trying to make money by partnering with platforms and AI model makers to sell their catalog for training or remixing features. Goldman Sachs estimates that by 2035, AI-related licensing tools and new monetization opportunities have the potential to improve record labels’ revenue by 10%.

articles.title: GTA 6 is the biggest PlayStation launch of all time
articles.text:
GTA 6 is the biggest PlayStation launch of all time
PS5 players logged 683 million hours of cumulative gameplay over its launch weekend.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest PlayStation launch in history, Sony Interactive Entertainment has revealed. It has set the record not just for the PS5, but for all five console generations released over the past three decades "across multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player titles." SIE's Tim Turi has announced that for the game's opening weekend ending on November 22, players logged 683 million hours of cumulative gameplay. Each player spent an average of 17.4 hours playing over those first four days.
Based on Sony's announcement, GTA 6 seems to have boosted PS5 sales, as the company saw the biggest number of new PS5 connections on a single day since the console was launched, outside of year-end holidays. The company said it was the first game accessed on 70 percent of all newly purchased and connected PS5 consoles over its launch weekend.
Overall, more than 39 million unique players booted up the game on the console. Sony didn't elaborate on how many of those players accessed the game over its launch weekend on a PS5 Pro. But it's worth noting that the company is experiencing a PS5 Pro shortage, and GTA 6's release was expected to make it even worse.
Rockstar Games released GTA 6 on November 19 for the PS5 and the Xbox Series X|S, 13 years after the launch of the franchise's fifth installment. It also did well and quickly became one of the most played games on the Xbox. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, announced that day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, calling it the "biggest entertainment launch in history." Despite the game's success, its developers are still apparently worried about the possibility of being impacted by layoffs currently sweeping across studios in the industry.

articles.title: TIDAL will delete 29 million AI-generated songs from its catalogue
articles.text:
TIDAL will begin deleting all wholly AI-generated tracks on December 9, about 29 million songs, and expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 more a day. It had already labelled and demonetised AI music in July, but says 43% of tracks it received in the past 90 days were AI-made.
TIDAL will start deleting every wholly AI-generated track from its catalogue on December 9, removing about 29 million songs. Robert Andersen, who leads TIDAL at parent company Block, announced the plan on X on Tuesday. TIDAL’s own account confirmed the date.
Andersen said the songs should be gone by the start of 2027. TIDAL also expects to turn away 80,000 to 85,000 AI-made tracks a day. He called it the first streaming service to take this step and urged rivals to follow.
In July, TIDAL began labelling AI tracks and cutting off their royalties. Andersen said that had not been enough.
“43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done,” Andersen wrote.
Most of that music finds no audience. Andersen said 96% of AI-generated songs on TIDAL get zero plays.
Rivals face the same flood. More than half the music uploaded to Deezer in June was made by AI.
Others have stopped short of deleting it. Spotify has pulled 50M spam tracks from its recommendations, but left them on the service. Apple Music has made AI tags mandatory for record companies.
The cut covers only songs made wholly by AI, which TIDAL finds with detection tools. Its terms of service warn those tools can wrongly tag tracks, and users can ask support to fix a label.

articles.title: Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch
articles.text:
Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed the companies to pull the human safety driver from behind the wheel.
The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027.
The milestone comes just 16 months after Uber announced an ambitious plan to launch a premium robotaxi service using Lucid electric vehicles outfitted with autonomous vehicle technology developed by startup Nuro.
That plan came with hefty investments in both companies and much-needed endorsements of their respective products. Uber initially agreed to invest $300 million in Lucid — a figure that has since ballooned to $500 million. Uber also agreed to invest nearly $500 million in Nuro, TechCrunch previously reported, citing sources familiar with the deal.
The agreement provided both Lucid and Nuro with boosts beyond the obvious capital injection. Uber agreed to buy at least 20,000 of Lucid Gravity SUVs over the next six years (a figure that later popped to at least 35,000 vehicles), giving the struggling EV maker a more predictable source of revenue. Nuro, meanwhile, was less than a year removed from announcing a risky, but necessary pivot away from developing driverless delivery vehicles and toward licensing its autonomous vehicle technology to automakers and mobility companies.
Nuro has spent nearly a year testing the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with a human safety operator behind the wheel. The California Department of Motor Vehicles, the agency that regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, granted Nuro a driverless AV permit in May 2026.
Uber and Nuro are also testing autonomous vehicles on public roads in Houston with human safety operators behind the wheel. Nuro is supplementing that on-road testing with closed-course testing and simulation to validate the self-driving system before opening the robotaxis to the public. The companies’ combined engineering fleet of autonomous vehicles, which stood at 100 AVs earlier this year, is expanding as Lucid begins manufacturing the first production versions of the robotaxis at its Arizona factory.
The Lucid Gravity robotaxi, unveiled in January 2026, is outfitted with high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar sensors, and radars that help the self-driving system perceive the real-world environment and operate in it. Uber, which will own and operate the fleet, has focused its efforts on the in-cabin experience, including how riders will interact with the vehicle.

articles.title: SCB có Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị mới
articles.text:
Ngày 23/11/2026, Phó Thống đốc Ngân hàng Nhà nước Phạm Tiến Dũng trao quyết định bổ nhiệm ông Phạm Quang Tiến, Tổng Giám đốc SCB giữ chức Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị ngân hàng này thay ông Phan Đình Điền nhận nhiệm vụ tại Agribank.
Ông Phạm Quang Tiến từng giữ Giám đốc chi nhánh BIDV Ba Tháng Hai (TP.HCM). Năm 2022 Ngân hàng Nhà nước chỉ định ông tham gia hội đồng quản trị SCB cùng với các nhân sự từ hệ thống ngân hàng thương mại nhà nước khi SCB bị đưa vào diện kiểm soát đặc biệt.
Trong quá trình làm việc tại SCB, ông Phạm Quang Tiến giữ chức Tổng Giám đốc tham gia điều hành và định hướng hoạt động tái cơ cấu, khai thác tài sản…
Tại buổi lễ, Phó Thống đốc Phạm Tiến Dũng yêu cầu tập thể Hội đồng quản trị, Ban điều hành SCB tiếp tục phát huy tinh thần đoàn kết, thống nhất, hoàn thành tốt nhiệm vụ được giao, đưa hoạt động của ngân hàng tiếp tục ổn định, bảo đảm an toàn, lành mạnh.
SCB bị đưa vào diện kiểm soát đặc biệt và đang trong giai đoạn tái cơ cấu kể từ năm 2022. Cho đến nay, những thông tin về kết quả kinh doanh cũng như tái cơ cấu của nhà băng này không được ngân hàng tiết lộ.
Tại buổi làm việc với Ngân hàng Nhà nước và các tổ chức tín dụng hồi tháng 8/2026, Thủ tướng Chính phủ Lê Minh Hưng yêu cầu đẩy mạnh tăng cường giám sát, kiểm soát các tổ chức tín dụng yếu kém đang kiểm soát đặc biệt, xử lý dứt điểm các ngân hàng yếu kém. Ngân hàng Nhà nước phối hợp với Bộ Tư pháp, Bộ Công an, Tòa án nhân dân tối cao, Viện Kiểm sát nhân dân tối cao để đẩy nhanh tiến độ triển khai phương án xử lý tài sản đảm bảo của Ngân hàng SCB.
Mới đây, SCB gây bất ngờ khi đồng loạt đưa lãi suất tiền gửi tất cả các kỳ hạn về 0%/năm. Điều này cho thấy thanh khoản của SCB giờ đây đang được NHNN hỗ trợ hoàn toàn.
Mặc dù đưa lãi suất huy động về 0%/năm nhưng SCB vẫn đang duy trì mức lãi suất cho vay cơ sở lên tới 13%/năm cho kỳ hạn 12 và 13 tháng, 12,82%/năm cho kỳ hạn trung và dài hạn.
Lãi suất cho vay cơ sở là cơ sở để ngân hàng áp dụng lãi suất cho vay thực tế đối với khách hàng, theo nguyên tắc lãi suất cho vay cơ sở cộng thêm biên độ lãi suất.
Trong khi đó, lãi suất cho vay bình quân do SCB công bố từ đầu năm 2026 đến nay vẫn duy trì quanh ngưỡng 5,4%/năm.
SCB cũng liên tục thông báo chấm dứt hoạt động của các phòng giao dịch trong 3 năm qua. Đến nay, đã có khoảng 200 phòng giao dịch của ngân hàng này dừng hoạt động, số phòng giao dịch đang hiện diện của ngân hàng này chỉ còn lại 8 phòng giao dịch.

articles.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
articles.text:
Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.
GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.
Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.
Some have managed to get the game to boot on PC, but recompiling the full game won’t be easy — even with help from AI tools like Claude. Take-Two is trying to slow this progress, and its IP enforcement team targeted the main GitHub repository for Leonida and more than 2,900 forks of it, claiming that it “infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.”
PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.
At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

articles.title: OpenAI employee who secretly recorded meetings allegedly affiliated with the Saudi government
articles.text:
OpenAI employee who secretly recorded meetings allegedly affiliated with the Saudi government
He uploaded recordings to Dropbox and took photos of confidential documents, prosecutors say.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, the OpenAI employee who was charged for hiding a recording device at OpenAI's headquarters, was allegedly "in frequent communication with various people affiliated with the Saudi government." The prosecutors have submitted a filing to ask the court to deny Alfozan's request for bail, according to Bloomberg, arguing that he might try to go back to his native Saudi Arabia due to his weak ties to the United States. They accused him of having links with the Saudi government in that filing.
Prosecutors also said that the authorities found hundreds of audio files in Alfozan's computer, dozens of which were recordings of meetings and conversations that took place at OpenAI throughout September 2026. Many of those recordings involved "what may be trade secrets," they said, and he uploaded some of them to Dropbox. Alfozan allegedly made AI-generated transcripts of the recordings, as well, categorizing them by date and renaming them based on their contents.
Alfozan was arrested in October after the company's staff discovered a recording device behind a TV in an executive conference room. He was fired on the same day. In addition to the recordings, authorities also apparently found images in Alfozan's phone of a "strategic partnership" document marked "confidential."
The former OpenAI employee denies he was stealing the company's trade secrets for Saudi and is asking the court to set a $1 million bond for him. Bloomberg says US District Judge Vince Chhabria is already doubting whether he should remain in custody without the evidence to support a more serious charge. Still, the court will hear his bond request today in San Francisco.

articles.title: Anthropic’s new Siren test tempts Claude to break out of its sandbox
articles.text:
Anthropic has published Siren, a test that tempts Claude agents to leave deliberately flawed sandboxes. Its newest models reached outside in 21% to 32% of scenarios but made clearly misaligned use of what they found in under 2%, against 25.8% for Mythos 5. Stating the sandbox rules in the system prompt cut reaching outside by 68% to 96%.
Anthropic’s newer Claude models will often reach out of a weak sandbox to finish a task, but rarely misuse what they find, the company said on Tuesday. The findings come from Siren, a new test it now runs on Claude models before release.
AI agents often work inside a sandbox, a walled-off space that limits the files, tools and networks they can reach. Siren gives them routine IT tasks in sandboxes with a deliberate flaw. Just outside sits something that would help, such as a file or a login.
Nothing in the more than 1,700 scenarios tells a model to leave or says it may. Instead, they add pressure, such as deadlines or orders to search thoroughly.
The Claude 5.5 series and Mythos 5.2 reached outside in 21% to 32% of scenarios. But they used what they found in ways no reasonable reading allowed in just 0.6% to 1.6%. For the older Mythos 5 and Mythos 5.1, that rate was 25.8% and 12.7%.
Anthropic says it does not fully know why newer models behave better, and none was trained on Siren. The models were tested without the safeguards they ship with. Anthropic stresses the rates do not reflect real-world use.
Escapes are not hypothetical. A Mythos preview escaped its sandbox in April and emailed a researcher.
In July, Anthropic said its models had breached three companies after a test setup was wrongly left online. OpenAI also paused a model that kept breaking out.
Simple fixes helped. Describing the sandbox and six rules for staying inside it in the system prompt made models 68% to 96% less likely to reach outside. A tool to report sandbox flaws also cut the rate.
Anthropic also tuned auto mode, which checks Claude’s commands before they run, on Siren. With all three fixes, misaligned use fell to almost zero, though two models finished about nine points fewer tasks.
Anthropic says sandboxes still need to be set up and patched properly. In July, researchers showed its own Cowork app could break out on Macs and read credentials.

articles.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
articles.text:
The problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year.
“Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.”
It’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants, but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster.
That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market.
“Global capacity of natural gas is only about 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, where solar is already at well over a terawatt,” he said. “Probably the most important lesson that we’ve learned over the last 20 years of backing companies is that Wright’s Law is the thing you want to leverage — making the same thing over and over again.”
Both solar and most forms of long-duration energy storage are built on small, modular technologies that can be manufactured at massive scale. “This is about speed and scale and economics, and we can win across all those dimensions,” Porter said.
G2VP had an early window into AI data center development, having led Crusoe’s Series C. “We’ve had a front-row seat at what’s been happening at that company, how they’ve evolved, how the different waves of data centers have evolved,” Porter said.
The venture firm estimates that data center investment will top $4 trillion until the end of the decade. As the next wave takes shape, the firm sees two different paths for data centers: small, on-grid facilities with their own generating capacity, and larger data centers powered by solar and long-duration energy storage.
“The big idea is to go off-grid,” Porter said. “What that would enable you to do is build with renewables in a way that’s independent of the grid. You can determine your own fate, go around some of the constraints of permitting, whether that’s access to the grid or air permits. You can accelerate your time to market dramatically.”
In recent years, energy storage has been synonymous with lithium-ion batteries, which are too expensive to compete with fossil fuels for round-the-clock power. But a new generation of long-duration energy storage products from the likes of Form Energy and G2VP portfolio company Antora Energy have brought the cost per megawatt-hour down significantly.
Even though the technologies might be a few years away from broad acceptance among data center developers, Porter said they should start thinking about them now.
“It’s analogous to surfing the biggest waves off of Mavericks here in Northern California. The wave is so big that you really have to be paddling and moving and be incredibly nimble to catch it. If you’re at a standstill, it’s just gonna blow you by,” he said.

articles.title: Kaszek closes $650M fund to back AI startups across Latin America
articles.text:
Kaszek Ventures has raised $650M for its seventh early-stage fund, which it says is the largest ever for Latin America. It will back 20 to 30 AI startups, mostly in Brazil and Mexico, at a time when only 14 venture funds have closed in the region this year.
Kaszek Ventures, Latin America’s largest venture capital firm, has raised $650M to back early-stage startups building with AI, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. The firm says it is the largest early-stage fund ever raised for the region.
The fund, Kaszek’s seventh for early-stage deals, beat its $600M target. Its last one, closed in 2023, raised $540M. Washington University in St. Louis and the Wellcome Trust are among the backers.
Kaszek plans to back 20 to 30 companies, starting at pre-seed and seed. It will keep about 60% of the money for their later rounds.
Most of the focus is on what Kaszek calls the “application layer” of AI. That means startups using language models in fields such as finance, health care and online marketplaces. Co-founder Hernán Kazah told Bloomberg he sees the most room in services for businesses.
“It’s a more natural fit for the types of problems that exist in Latin America,” Kazah said. Many firms there still rely on manual processes, he added, and services can be costly or hard to reach.
The fund is also looking at AI infrastructure such as data centres and chips. Kazah pointed to the region’s energy, land and closeness to the US. Power shortages, though, have held back data centres in Mexico.
Brazil and Mexico will stay its biggest markets, with Argentina and Colombia on the rise. Kaszek was founded in 2011 by former MercadoLibre executives Kazah and Nicolas Szekasy. Its portfolio includes digital bank Nubank, QuintoAndar and Kavak.
The raise stands out in a weak market. PitchBook ranks it the largest Latin America-focused venture fund to close since 2023. Only 14 venture funds closed in the region through September, it says, against 68 in all of 2023.
AI startups can still draw big cheques, though. In August, Brazil’s Decade, an AI wealth adviser built by former Nubank staff, raised an $85M seed round.
